question: What does reproductive health mean beyond simply being free from disease?

options.A: The total eradication of maternal mortality in rural communities
options.B: Ensuring every woman gives birth to at least four children
options.C: Having access to free maternity drugs in public health facilities
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health encompasses holistic well-being across physical, mental, and social dimensions, not just the physical absence of illness. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h1)

question: How does the modern definition of reproductive health influence the daily work of a midwife?

options.A: It restricts her responsibilities strictly to managing normal deliveries
options.B: It shifts her primary duty to treating newborn infections only
options.C: It requires her to focus exclusively on family planning commodities
options.D: It guides care to cover overall well-being and personal reproductive choices

explanation: Because reproductive health involves safe sex, reproductive capability, and personal choice, midwives must look beyond the physical body to support overall wellness and autonomy. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h1)

question: What major shift in global health policy occurred at the 1994 Cairo Conference?

options.A: Mandating a specific number of children per family across developing nations
options.B: Banning traditional birth attendants from assisting rural deliveries
options.C: Moving from demographic population control to individual reproductive rights
options.D: Establishing the first global guidelines for managing postpartum haemorrhage

explanation: The Cairo Conference famously shifted the global focus away from strict population number targets and onto human rights and individual empowerment. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why was the shift introduced at the Cairo Conference especially important for women?

options.A: It recognised their autonomy, health, and rights as central to development
options.B: It transferred all leadership roles in hospitals strictly to female staff
options.C: It guaranteed them free tertiary education in all developing countries
options.D: It eliminated the need for antenatal checkups during normal pregnancies

explanation: By placing women's rights and health at the centre of the agenda, the conference ensured that healthcare systems would support personal choice rather than force demographic targets. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which group is included in the broad scope of reproductive health services besides women of childbearing age?

options.A: Adolescents, men, and older adults
options.B: Only newborn babies under one month old
options.C: Strictly retired civil servants
options.D: Exclusively male patients over fifty

explanation: Reproductive health spans the entire life cycle and involves all members of the community, including men, adolescents, and older individuals. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h3)

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach activity. Which action fits best within the scope of reproductive health services?

options.A: Treating chronic hypertension and stroke in elderly patients
options.B: Administering mass vaccination against polio for infants
options.C: Providing counselling on family planning and screening for sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Conducting routine dental checks for primary school children

explanation: Family planning and infection screening are core components of reproductive health services. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is required for reproductive health services to be properly delivered at the primary health care level?

options.A: Mandatory hospitalization for every pregnant woman
options.B: Exclusively private funding from international donors
options.C: Strictly high-tech surgical theaters in every village clinic
options.D: Availability, accessibility, acceptability, and good quality

explanation: Health service delivery standards require that care be accessible, available, acceptable to the local culture, and maintained at a high standard of quality. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why are functioning referral pathways essential for reproductive health care delivery?

options.A: They allow primary clinics to transfer all routine antenatal work away
options.B: They prevent midwives from ever performing normal vaginal deliveries
options.C: They eliminate the need for community health education programmes
options.D: They ensure women with severe complications reach higher-level facilities quickly

explanation: Quick and efficient referral systems save lives when unexpected obstetric emergencies arise that primary clinics cannot manage. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h4)

question: How can a Nigerian midwife best respect reproductive rights in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: By forcing every client to accept the same family planning method
options.B: By ensuring informed consent, patient confidentiality, and bodily autonomy
options.C: By ignoring local cultural beliefs completely during consultations
options.D: By restricting health education strictly to married women over thirty

explanation: Respecting reproductive rights requires upholding the client's right to make private, informed choices about their own body and health. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge a midwife might face when applying the Cairo framework in Nigeria?

options.A: Navigating complex cultural and religious values regarding family planning
options.B: Addressing high rates of teenage pregnancy and unsafe abortion
options.C: An immediate excess of fully equipped tertiary hospitals in every rural ward
options.D: Overcoming structural and economic barriers in primary health care

explanation: Rural areas in Nigeria typically face a shortage, not an excess, of well-equipped health facilities, making this statement incorrect. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the most important rule for a midwife when caring for mothers in labor?

options.A: Dignity and respect without discrimination
options.B: Strict adherence to hospital financial quotas
options.C: Limiting patient movement during early labor
options.D: Prioritizing the doctor over the patient always

explanation: Every client has a human right to receive fair and equal care, no matter their background or status. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why should we treat mothers as active partners in their own healthcare?

options.A: It speeds up the discharge process for the ward
options.B: It ensures patients make choices about their bodies
options.C: It frees the midwife from all legal responsibility
options.D: It prevents patients from asking questions about drugs

explanation: When clients participate actively, we respect their personal autonomy and involve them in decisions about their treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h1)

question: What do we call human rights that can never be taken away or given up?

options.A: Indivisibility
options.B: Inalienability
options.C: Universality
options.D: Accountability

explanation: Inalienable rights belong to every human being inherently and cannot be stripped away. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h2)

question: How does the rule of non-discrimination apply on a busy labor ward?

options.A: Patients who pay cash upfront get faster surgical theaters
options.B: Hospital staff decide who is worthy of pain relief based on tribe
options.C: Every woman receives equal attention regardless of social class
options.D: Midwives can prioritize relatives over regular community members

explanation: Non-discrimination means no patient is treated differently because of their wealth, social standing, or background. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is guaranteed under sexual and reproductive health rights?

options.A: State control over maternity ward admissions
options.B: Automatic authorization for major surgeries
options.C: Mandatory family size limits for all citizens
options.D: Freedom from coercion and violence

explanation: These rights protect individuals from being forced or pressured when making choices about their reproductive health. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h3)

question: A young woman asks a health worker for family planning, but is refused because she is unmarried. Which right is violated?

options.A: The right to choose her own attending obstetrician
options.B: The right to emergency surgical intervention
options.C: The right to non-discrimination and health information
options.D: The right to free hospitalization during pregnancy

explanation: Refusing care or information based on a client's marital status breaches non-discrimination principles. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which international treaty specifically protects women's health and rights in Africa?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Maputo Protocol
options.C: The Nuremberg Code
options.D: The Geneva Convention

explanation: The Maputo Protocol is a key African human rights agreement focused on women's health and bodily integrity. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h4)

question: What major change did the 1994 ICPD Cairo conference bring to global reproductive health?

options.A: Focusing on individual rights rather than rigid population control targets
options.B: Making all hospital deliveries mandatory across every continent
options.C: Eliminating the need for trained midwives in rural communities
options.D: Giving governments total control over family sizing decisions

explanation: The Cairo conference shifted the focus from government numbers to personal human agency, dignity, and health rights. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a direct human rights violation by a healthcare provider?

options.A: Recording vital signs every thirty minutes in the active phase
options.B: Demanding illegal bribes before rendering emergency obstetric care
options.C: Advising a client on the benefits of exclusive breastfeeding
options.D: Asking a patient about her medical history during booking

explanation: Withholding emergency care for financial gain breaches the duty of care and human rights obligations. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do government responsibilities for health rights translate to everyday healthcare facilities?

options.A: Providing well-equipped facilities and trained personnel
options.B: Allowing private hospitals to set their own medical laws
options.C: Removing supervision from rural primary health centers
options.D: Exempting health workers from all local legal liabilities

explanation: The government fulfills its health obligation by ensuring that clinics have proper infrastructure, supplies, and trained staff. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does 'bodily autonomy' mean for a woman in labor?

options.A: The right to make decisions about her own body without force
options.B: The requirement to give birth without pharmacological pain relief
options.C: The obligation to accept any surgical procedure ordered
options.D: The duty to obey all instructions given by the senior nurse

explanation: Bodily autonomy means an individual keeps total ownership and decision-making power over their own physical self. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which action violates a client's right to informed consent during childbirth?

options.A: Performing an episiotomy without telling or asking the patient
options.B: Asking permission before conducting a routine vaginal examination
options.C: Explaining the risks and benefits of oxytocin augmentation first
options.D: Waiting for a patient to sign a consent form before a Cesarean section

explanation: Doing an invasive procedure without the patient's knowledge and permission is a breach of bodily integrity. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to rights-based maternity care in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural norms that discourage women from questioning elders
options.B: Severe infrastructural deficits in primary health centers
options.C: Excessive availability of modern medical equipment
options.D: Burnout among overworked and underpaid healthcare staff

explanation: A lack of equipment, rather than an excess of it, is a major challenge in providing quality care. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h7)

question: How can an individual midwife promote rights-based care despite difficult working conditions?

options.A: By charging extra consultation fees to cover hospital shortages
options.B: By practicing respectful maternity care and educating clients
options.C: By refusing to attend to patients from outside her ethnic group
options.D: By ignoring hospital protocols when working night shifts

explanation: Midwives make a huge difference simply by treating clients with respect and empowering them through health education. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main difference between sex and gender in health education?

options.A: Sex is determined by society while gender is purely genetic
options.B: Sex refers to biological traits while gender refers to socially constructed roles
options.C: Gender only applies to women while sex applies to men
options.D: Sex and gender mean the exact same thing in clinical practice

explanation: Sex points to physical and biological differences, whereas gender describes the cultural and social expectations built around being male or female. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must a midwife look beyond the individual patient when assessing barriers to maternal care?

options.A: Midwives are legally required to interview the entire extended family
options.B: Individual patients never know what kind of treatment they need
options.C: Biological sex is the only factor that ever affects clinic attendance
options.D: Household and community power imbalances heavily influence health decisions

explanation: Health choices in many communities are shaped by family dynamics and social expectations rather than just the personal desire of the pregnant woman. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common result of women's economic dependence in some communities?

options.A: Automatic exemption from all household agricultural duties
options.B: Inability to easily pay for transport and medical tests
options.C: Total control over major family land and housing sales
options.D: Immediate free access to specialized private hospitals

explanation: When women lack independent income, paying for essential care like drugs and transport becomes dependent on another family member's approval and funds. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h2)

question: How can heavy domestic workloads negatively impact a pregnant woman's health?

options.A: They ensure she gets adequate cardiovascular exercise daily
options.B: They automatically increase her biological resistance to infections
options.C: They delay her from seeking timely antenatal care and rest
options.D: They eliminate all forms of stress during the third trimester

explanation: Endless household chores consume a pregnant woman's time and energy, often preventing her from resting or attending clinic appointments promptly. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is a frequent barrier when family planning advice is given exclusively to the female client?

options.A: She may lack the household authority to implement the method without partner consent
options.B: Hospitals forbid women from discussing modern medicine with their spouses
options.C: Midwives are legally barred from distributing commodities to married women
options.D: Biological contraceptives only work if the male partner swallows them

explanation: Without partner involvement or decision-making power, women often face severe social risks or lack resources to use reproductive health services openly. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why might a male partner react negatively to a request for family planning in some settings?

options.A: He knows that modern contraceptives are chemically identical to herbal teas
options.B: He wants to ensure every pregnancy results in twins or triplets
options.C: He may incorrectly equate fertility control with marital infidelity or loss of status
options.D: He is usually the primary person who suffers from morning sickness

explanation: Misconceptions about family planning often tie large family sizes to a man's pride, community standing, and fidelity suspicions. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which model explains how delays in seeking, reaching, and receiving care lead to poor outcomes?

options.A: The gender equality index
options.B: The obstetric triage formula
options.C: The three delays model
options.D: The primary healthcare matrix

explanation: The three delays model highlights how decision-making delays, transport hurdles, and facility shortcomings contribute to maternal mortality. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h4)

question: A pregnant woman presents with severe anemia and exhaustion because her household culture dictates that men eat the most nutritious food first. Which factor is primarily at play?

options.A: An acute allergic reaction to standard antenatal iron supplements
options.B: Gender inequity affecting household nutritional distribution
options.C: A rare genetic blood disorder inherited from her parents
options.D: Natural physiological changes that occur in every normal pregnancy

explanation: Unequal food distribution based on gender roles directly deprives pregnant women of essential nutrients, leading to preventable conditions like severe anemia. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does inviting male partners to special antenatal sessions improve maternal outcomes?

options.A: It proves that women are incapable of remembering their own drug schedules
options.B: It transforms partners into supporters who recognize pregnancy danger signs
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for professional midwives in the clinic
options.D: It allows men to take over the clinical examination of pregnant women

explanation: Involving men helps secure financial and logistical support for the mother, ensuring rapid action if complications arise. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h5)

question: A midwife notices that many women in a rural clinic miss follow-up visits because their husbands refuse to give transport money. What is the most practical first step for the midwife?

options.A: Charge the women double fees so they learn to demand money from their partners
options.B: Organize community awareness meetings with local leaders to involve men in maternal health
options.C: Advise the women to stop attending antenatal care entirely to avoid domestic conflict
options.D: Report every single husband in the community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Engaging community leaders and male partners directly helps dismantle barriers at the household level and builds local support for women's healthcare. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main root cause of gender-based violence in society?

options.A: Genetically predetermined aggressive instincts
options.B: Economic stability within family structures
options.C: Systemic power imbalances between genders
options.D: Lack of formal education among victims

explanation: Gender-based violence stems primarily from unequal power relations and socially constructed gender roles that disadvantage women and girls. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why should midwives view gender-based violence as a public health issue rather than just a private matter?

options.A: It allows the hospital to generate revenue from legal fees
options.B: Government policies mandate that doctors handle all domestic disputes
options.C: Private matters are illegal to discuss during routine antenatal care
options.D: It causes widespread physical and psychological harm requiring healthcare

explanation: Because violence significantly damages physical and mental well-being, healthcare providers treat it with the same clinical seriousness as infectious disease or obstetric complications. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common social or cultural driver of gender-based violence in many communities?

options.A: Enforcement of strict female financial independence
options.B: Strict patriarchal authority within the household
options.C: Cultural practices that enforce silence and secrecy
options.D: Economic dependency of women on their partners

explanation: Financial independence generally reduces vulnerability, whereas economic dependency and patriarchal control are the actual drivers of abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h2)

question: How does economic dependency make it harder for a victim to leave an abusive relationship?

options.A: It prevents healthcare workers from providing clinical examinations
options.B: It leaves the victim without the financial resources needed for basic survival
options.C: It automatically grants legal custody of all children to the abuser
options.D: It stops local police stations from filing formal incident reports

explanation: Without money, housing, or food of their own, victims struggle immensely to break away from an abusive partner. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h2)

question: What type of abuse involves withholding financial resources and controlling access to money?

options.A: Institutional violence
options.B: Psychological abuse
options.C: Physical violence
options.D: Economic abuse

explanation: Economic abuse specifically targets a person's financial autonomy and ability to sustain themselves independently. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h3)

question: A patient shares that her husband constantly threatens to abandon her and humiliates her publicly, though he has never hit her. What category of abuse does this represent?

options.A: Harmful traditional practice
options.B: Economic deprivation
options.C: Psychological abuse
options.D: Physical violence

explanation: Threats, public humiliation, and intimidation are classic indicators of psychological or emotional abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is a frequent long-term physical consequence of sexual violence reported by women in clinics?

options.A: Permanent elevation of natural visual acuity
options.B: Complete immunity to common bacterial pathogens
options.C: Sudden increase in overall bone density
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain and recurrent infections

explanation: Trauma and forced intercourse commonly lead to lasting gynecological issues, including chronic pain and persistent infections. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do many survivors of gender-based violence delay seeking medical attention for their injuries?

options.A: Strict hospital policies forbidding treatment of trauma
options.B: Fear of social stigma, shame, and further retaliation
options.C: Lack of interest in personal health maintenance
options.D: Belief that physical injuries heal instantly on their own

explanation: Stigma, fear of being blamed, and threats from the abuser often force victims to hide their injuries and avoid clinics. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why are antenatal and postnatal clinics ideal settings for identifying survivors of gender-based violence?

options.A: Clinics are completely free from cultural biases and stigma
options.B: Midwives are legally required to arrest suspected abusers on site
options.C: Patients are always accompanied by independent legal counsel
options.D: Women attend these clinics regularly during pregnancy and after birth

explanation: Routine maternity care brings women into contact with health workers multiple times, creating opportunities to build trust and screen for abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h5)

question: A male partner insists on answering all questions for his pregnant wife and refuses to leave the consultation room. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: A medical requirement mandated by the national health ministry
options.B: Potential controlling behavior and a red flag for possible gender-based violence
options.C: Standard supportive behavior expected of all expectant fathers
options.D: An indication that the patient has excellent mental health

explanation: An overly dominant partner who refuses to leave the patient alone often uses isolation and control, which are core indicators of abuse. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the core focus of trauma-informed care for survivors of violence?

options.A: Asking what happened to the patient instead of what is wrong with them
options.B: Forcing the patient to report the abuser to the police immediately
options.C: Ignoring past trauma to focus strictly on physical symptoms
options.D: Leaving clinical decisions entirely up to the hospital director

explanation: Trauma-informed care looks at symptoms through the lens of lived experience and past trauma rather than viewing the patient as defective. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is it unhelpful to force a survivor into taking immediate legal action against their abuser?

options.A: It prevents the midwife from documenting physical injuries properly
options.B: It violates international nursing licensing regulations and bylaws
options.C: It guarantees that the abuser will apologize and change their behavior
options.D: It can strip away their sense of control and cause further psychological trauma

explanation: Survivors need autonomy and control over their choices; pressuring them mimics the powerlessness of the abuse itself. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which Nigerian law provides significant legal protections against domestic and gender-based violence?

options.A: Standard Public Health Quarantine Regulation
options.B: Federal Road Safety Commission Decree
options.C: National Minimum Wage and Labor Act
options.D: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act

explanation: The VAPP Act is a key legal instrument in Nigeria designed to eliminate violence in private and public life. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for supporting a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: No single profession can meet the complex medical, legal, and social needs of the survivor
options.B: Social workers handle all clinical diagnoses of physical trauma
options.C: Midwives are legally prohibited from speaking with victims of violence alone
options.D: Hospital administrative rules require at least five staff members per patient

explanation: Recovery requires medical care, psychological support, social services, and legal protection, which only a coordinated team can provide. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the medical benefit of performing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhancing natural hormonal balance
options.B: Treating congenital birth defects
options.C: Preventing pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: There are no medical benefits

explanation: FGM has no health benefits and is performed purely for cultural or social reasons. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do many communities in Nigeria continue to practice FGM despite public health campaigns?

options.A: It permanently cures chronic reproductive tract infections
options.B: It is required by modern national health policies
options.C: It is viewed as a vital cultural tradition and rite of passage
options.D: Doctors recommend it to prevent infant mortality

explanation: Deep-seated social norms and traditions drive the continuation of FGM to ensure social acceptance and marriageability. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which type of FGM involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a covering seal?

options.A: Type III
options.B: Type II
options.C: Type IV
options.D: Type I

explanation: Type III infibulation involves cutting and repositioning the labia to create a restrictive seal over the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h2)

question: What does Type I FGM specifically involve?

options.A: Total stitching of the vaginal opening
options.B: Excision of both labia minora and majora
options.C: Scraping and cauterization of the vulva
options.D: Removal of the clitoris and/or prepuce

explanation: Type I clitoridectomy focuses on the partial or complete removal of the clitoral structure and its fold of skin. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is an immediate physical complication of FGM?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Development of uterine fibroids

explanation: The cutting of highly vascular genital tissue without medical supervision frequently leads to heavy bleeding and shock. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h3)

question: A woman with Type III FGM is admitted in active second stage of labor. What specific intervention will she likely need for a safe delivery?

options.A: Immediate cesarean section
options.B: Manual vacuum aspiration
options.C: Routine fundal pressure
options.D: Surgical deinfibulation

explanation: The scar tissue covering the vaginal opening must be surgically opened to allow the baby to pass safely. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is trauma-informed care essential when examining a woman who has undergone FGM?

options.A: To speed up the healing of surgical episiotomy scars
options.B: To prevent triggering severe anxiety or painful emotional flashbacks
options.C: To eliminate the need for local anesthesia during delivery
options.D: To guarantee complete reversal of past tissue damage

explanation: Trauma-informed care respects the patient's emotional history and helps build trust during sensitive clinical examinations. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a primary role of the midwife during antenatal booking for an FGM survivor?

options.A: Arranging immediate referral for cosmetic genital surgery
options.B: Reporting family members to local law enforcement
options.C: Discussing anticipated birth challenges and birth plans
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics throughout pregnancy

explanation: Antenatal discussions help prepare the midwife and mother for any surgical needs, such as deinfibulation, during delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which Nigerian legislative act explicitly prohibits the practice of Female Genital Mutilation at the federal level?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: Child Nutrition and Welfare Act
options.D: Midwifery and Nursing Council Decree

explanation: The VAPP Act provides the federal legal backing to prosecute individuals who perform or promote FGM in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is community sensitization by midwives considered critical alongside legal prohibitions?

options.A: Community meetings replace the need for hospital-based deliveries
options.B: Traditional leaders refuse to obey federal court orders
options.C: Midwives are legally mandated to act as police investigators
options.D: Laws alone cannot change deep-seated cultural beliefs without education

explanation: True behavioral change happens when community members understand the health harms and voluntarily abandon the practice. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T5#BMP310_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the recognized age threshold below which a marriage is classified as child marriage?

options.A: Under the age of eighteen years
options.B: Below twenty-one years of age
options.C: Under the age of sixteen years
options.D: Below fifteen years of age

explanation: International standards and Nigerian legal frameworks define any marriage involving a person under eighteen as child marriage. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is it important for midwives to understand the cultural context of child marriage in Nigeria?

options.A: It ensures they can fine families who break customary laws
options.B: It allows them to personally change federal marriage legislation
options.C: It replaces the need for clinical obstetric care training
options.D: It helps them engage communities without causing unnecessary resistance

explanation: Understanding local beliefs allows healthcare workers to approach sensitive topics respectfully and build trust rather than alienating the community. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is a main economic reason behind child marriage in struggling households?

options.A: Investing in large-scale commercial farming
options.B: Alleviating financial strain and securing bride price
options.C: Complying with mandatory modern taxation laws
options.D: Funding the secondary education of younger siblings

explanation: Impoverished families sometimes view early marriage as a survival strategy to reduce household expenses and gain financial support. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h2)

question: How do community conflicts and insecurity influence the rate of early marriage?

options.A: Traditional marriage ceremonies become completely free of cost
options.B: Governments officially mandate early marriage to boost population growth
options.C: Schools close permanently, making marriage the only legal option for housing
options.D: Parents may marry off daughters early believing marriage provides physical protection

explanation: During conflicts or displacement, families often fear for their daughters' safety and look to marriage as a safeguard against violence. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why are young adolescent mothers especially at risk of obstructed labor?

options.A: Their babies are always born with congenital bone disorders
options.B: They consume a diet that is strictly deficient in clean water
options.C: They routinely refuse all forms of skilled birth attendance
options.D: Their pelvic bones are not yet fully grown or developed

explanation: An underdeveloped pelvis creates a mechanical barrier to the passage of the baby, leading to obstructed labor. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h3)

question: A thirteen-year-old first-time mother comes to the clinic with continuous urine leakage after a difficult home delivery. What condition does this history suggest?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Obstetric fistula

explanation: Continuous leakage of urine following prolonged obstructed labor in a young mother is the classic presentation of an obstetric fistula. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is one of the most immediate social consequences for a young girl who enters into child marriage?

options.A: Automatic exemption from community taxation
options.B: Instantaneous financial independence from her family
options.C: Immediate appointment to local political office
options.D: Withdrawal and dropping out of formal education

explanation: Child marriage almost always forces girls out of school, cutting short their education and future employment opportunities. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h4)

question: How does early marriage primarily affect a young girl's mental and emotional well-being?

options.A: It guarantees lifelong emotional resilience against trauma
options.B: It often causes severe isolation, anxiety, and depressive symptoms
options.C: It builds strong leadership confidence through early adult responsibilities
options.D: It eliminates all forms of everyday adolescent stress

explanation: The sudden loss of childhood, forced sexual relations, and social isolation leave young brides vulnerable to deep psychological distress. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which Nigerian legislation sets the legal minimum age of marriage at eighteen years?

options.A: The Criminal Code Act
options.B: The Midwifery Registration Decree
options.C: The National Health Act
options.D: The Child Rights Act

explanation: The Child Rights Act domesticates international treaties and specifies eighteen as the minimum age for marriage and criminal responsibility. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why does the enforcement of laws against child marriage remain inconsistent across Nigeria?

options.A: International treaties prevent local police from intervening in family matters
options.B: The federal government abolished all marriage laws in the year two thousand
options.C: Midwives have sole legal authority to prosecute offenders in local courts
options.D: State-level adoption varies and customary or religious laws sometimes conflict with federal acts

explanation: Because family law and customary practices are heavily influenced by state legislation and local traditions, enforcement is uneven across the country. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h5)

question: A twelve-year-old girl is brought to the antenatal clinic pregnant and visibly distressed. What is the most appropriate initial action for the midwife?

options.A: Scold the young patient for engaging in premarital relationships
options.B: Turn her away immediately because she is underage for standard clinic registration
options.C: Report her family to the local media for public shaming and deterrence
options.D: Provide compassionate, specialized clinical care while involving social protection services

explanation: Midwives prioritize clinical safety and psychological support while collaborating with social welfare systems to protect vulnerable minors. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of a midwife in addressing child marriage?

options.A: Educating communities and schools about the health risks of early unions
options.B: Collaborating with social workers to safeguard vulnerable adolescents
options.C: Providing specialized antenatal and intrapartum care for young mothers
options.D: Presiding over customary court trials to sentence offenders to prison

explanation: Midwives are healthcare providers and advocates, not judges or legal magistrates responsible for criminal sentencing. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main root cause of gender-based violence in communities?

options.A: A lack of modern technological advancement
options.B: Seasonal economic fluctuations in markets
options.C: Strict adherence to universal health laws
options.D: Unequal power dynamics between genders

explanation: Gender-based violence is fundamentally rooted in unequal power relations and patriarchal structures that perpetuate control over women and girls. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of intimate partner violence?

options.A: A community dispute over farmland ownership boundaries
options.B: Physical or psychological harm inflicted by a current spouse
options.C: Neglect of an elderly patient by a hospital attendant
options.D: Robbery committed by an unknown person on the street

explanation: Intimate partner violence specifically involves harmful acts committed by someone with whom the survivor shares or has shared a domestic or romantic relationship. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which physical sign during pregnancy should make a midwife suspect intimate partner violence?

options.A: Bilateral swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Mild elevation in baseline blood pressure
options.C: Bruises located on the abdomen or breasts
options.D: Moderate physiological weight gain

explanation: Injuries directed at the central areas of the body, such as the abdomen and breasts, are strong warning signs of trauma inflicted by another person. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h2)

question: A pregnant woman keeps coming to clinic late, looks frightened, and has unexplained pelvic pain. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Document her behavior as uncooperative and discharge her care
options.B: Prescribe strong analgesics and send her home immediately
options.C: Instruct her partner to wait outside during all future visits
options.D: Provide a private, safe space to gently ask about abuse at home

explanation: Creating a confidential environment allows the midwife to explore underlying safety issues when behavioral and physical red flags are present. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main goal of trauma-informed care in clinical practice?

options.A: Focusing solely on immediate surgical repair of physical wounds
options.B: Understanding what happened to the patient to avoid re-traumatization
options.C: Ensuring the patient follows every hospital rule without question
options.D: Convincing the patient to press legal charges immediately

explanation: Trauma-informed care centers on understanding past trauma to prevent clinical procedures or interactions from triggering further distress. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which statement shows that a midwife is using trauma-informed communication?

options.A: "You just need to forget the past and focus on your baby."
options.B: "If you had left earlier, you would not be in this situation."
options.C: "Why did you wait so long before coming to the clinic?"
options.D: "I believe you, and none of this is your fault."

explanation: Validating the survivor's experience and removing blame fosters trust and emotional safety. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which medical treatment must be offered quickly after a recent sexual assault to help prevent HIV transmission?

options.A: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
options.B: Routine broad-spectrum multivitamins
options.C: Therapeutic blood transfusion
options.D: Long-term injectable contraceptives

explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should be administered as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of exposure, to reduce the risk of HIV transmission. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is it important to write down the patient's exact words during a forensic assessment?

options.A: It preserves objective facts and legal integrity for potential legal proceedings
options.B: It replaces the need for a physical examination of the injuries
options.C: It guarantees that the perpetrator will be arrested within twenty-four hours
options.D: It fulfills hospital administrative filing quotas for insurance claims

explanation: Precise documentation of injuries and statements ensures reliable evidence if the survivor decides to pursue legal action. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the name of the Nigerian federal law that criminalizes domestic violence and harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Criminal Code and Penal Code Consolidation Law
options.B: Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) (VAPP) Act
options.C: Midwives Registration and Practice Decree
options.D: National Health Insurance Authority Act

explanation: The VAPP Act is the landmark federal legislation designed to eliminate violence in private and public life, prohibiting offenses like domestic abuse and harmful practices. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h5)

question: How can midwives help survivors who need legal protection?

options.A: By arresting the alleged perpetrator within the hospital premises
options.B: By issuing legally binding protection orders directly from the clinic
options.C: By connecting survivors to legal aid services and social support agencies
options.D: By serving as the official prosecuting attorneys in court trials

explanation: While midwives do not provide legal services themselves, they play a crucial bridging role by linking survivors to appropriate legal and social support networks. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using a multi-sectoral referral pathway for gender-based violence survivors?

options.A: To ensure the hospital receives financial compensation from the government
options.B: To connect health, legal, social, and security services for comprehensive care
options.C: To reduce the total number of patient visits required at the facility
options.D: To transfer all administrative duties away from the primary healthcare clinic

explanation: A multi-sectoral approach ensures that medical, psychological, legal, and safety needs are all addressed through coordinated agency collaboration. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h6)

question: A survivor of severe domestic violence needs a safe place to stay tonight because her partner threatened her life. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Tell her to sleep in the hospital waiting area indefinitely until morning
options.B: Advise her to return home and try to resolve the argument peacefully
options.C: Coordinate with a verified safe shelter or social welfare service with the patient's consent
options.D: Call the local newspaper to expose the partner publicly and shame him

explanation: Immediate physical safety is paramount, and linking the survivor to a designated shelter with her consent protects her from ongoing danger. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h6)

question: When is a midwife generally required to break patient confidentiality and report an incident?

options.A: When the survivor is a minor below the legal age of consent
options.B: When the hospital administrator asks for general clinic statistics
options.C: When a family member demands to know the medical diagnosis
options.D: When a journalist requests details for a public news report

explanation: Child protection laws require healthcare providers to report abuse involving minors to safeguard vulnerable children. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is it crucial to respect an adult survivor's autonomy when managing their care?

options.A: It ensures that the perpetrator automatically receives a prison sentence
options.B: It empowers survivors to control decisions regarding their own safety and legal steps
options.C: It allows the midwife to avoid taking any clinical notes about the visit
options.D: It protects the hospital from any financial liability during court trials

explanation: Respecting adult autonomy ensures the survivor is not subjected to further loss of control, allowing them to lead decisions about reporting and recovery. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h7)

question: Where do the organisms that cause endogenous reproductive tract infections primarily come from?

options.A: Bacterial contamination from improperly sterilized surgical tools
options.B: Microbes that already live naturally inside the vagina
options.C: Waterborne parasites acquired from swimming in stagnant pools
options.D: Pathogens transmitted exclusively through sexual intercourse

explanation: Endogenous infections happen when microbes that normally live inside the vagina start to overgrow because the local environment changes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it helpful to know the difference between an endogenous infection and a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Only sexually transmitted infections can cause visible changes in vaginal discharge
options.B: Only STIs cause symptoms that result in psychological distress for the patient
options.C: Endogenous infections are always permanent while STIs can be easily cured
options.D: Endogenous infections do not typically require routine partner treatment like STIs do

explanation: Knowing an infection is endogenous saves the patient from unnecessary blame or partner tracing, since these issues come from internal balance shifts rather than outside transmission. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which helpful bacteria group is mostly responsible for keeping the vaginal environment healthy and acidic?

options.A: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Lactobacilli
options.C: Candida albicans
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: Lactobacilli are the good bacteria that dominate a healthy vagina. They produce lactic acid to keep the pH low and protect against harmful overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h2)

question: What happens to the vaginal pH when the number of protective Lactobacilli drops a lot?

options.A: It remains perfectly stable because the cervix regulates the pH
options.B: It shifts entirely to a neutral balance that supports normal tissue repair
options.C: It becomes extremely acidic, killing off all bacteria completely
options.D: It becomes less acidic, which encourages harmful microbes to grow

explanation: When lactic acid goes down, the vaginal pH rises above 4.5. This creates an easy environment for bad microbes to multiply. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which common practice washes away protective bacteria and raises vaginal pH?

options.A: Wearing loose cotton underwear
options.B: Eating high-fiber local foods
options.C: Drinking plenty of clean water
options.D: Frequent vaginal douching

explanation: Douching disrupts the natural balance by washing away helpful Lactobacilli and introducing fluids that neutralize vaginal acidity. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h3)

question: How can taking broad-spectrum antibiotics lead to yeast infections or bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: By changing the systemic blood pressure of the reproductive organs
options.B: By increasing the production of glycogen in the vaginal walls
options.C: By killing protective Lactobacilli alongside harmful bacteria
options.D: By directly stimulating the rapid growth of yeast and anaerobic microbes

explanation: Antibiotics wipe out the friendly bacteria that normally keep other microbes in check, leaving an open path for overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h3)

question: What kind of vaginal discharge is most typical for a yeast infection (vulvovaginal candidiasis)?

options.A: Thick, white, and curdy like cottage cheese
options.B: Clear, watery, and completely odorless
options.C: Thin, gray-white with a strong fishy odor
options.D: Yellow, frothy, and foul-smelling

explanation: Yeast infections usually show up with a thick, white, cottage cheese-like discharge along with severe itching and irritation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient has a thin gray vaginal discharge and a noticeable fishy odor that gets worse after sex. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.B: Bacterial vaginosis
options.C: Trichomoniasis
options.D: Gonococcal cervicitis

explanation: A thin gray discharge with a fishy smell, especially when semen makes the odor stronger, points directly to bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h4)

question: What finding under a microscope is a key sign of bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Gram-negative diplococci
options.B: Motile trichomonads
options.C: Clue cells
options.D: Fungal hyphae

explanation: Clue cells are vaginal skin cells covered in so many bacteria that their edges look fuzzy and unclear, which points to bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: During a speculum exam, why do midwives perform a whiff test using 10 percent potassium hydroxide?

options.A: To stain the bacterial cell walls for easy microscopic counting
options.B: To measure the exact acidity level of the vaginal walls
options.C: To kill off unwanted parasites before collecting laboratory samples
options.D: To release volatile amines that produce a distinct fishy odor

explanation: Potassium hydroxide reacts with the chemical byproducts of bacterial overgrowth, releasing a strong fishy smell that helps confirm bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which medication is commonly given first to treat bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Benzathine penicillin
options.B: Artemether-lumefantrine
options.C: Metronidazole
options.D: Fluconazole

explanation: Metronidazole is the standard first-line medicine because it works very well against the anaerobic bacteria causing bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is treating male sexual partners usually NOT needed when a woman is treated for bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Clinical trials show partner treatment does not prevent the infection from returning
options.B: The medications used to treat women are completely toxic to male physiology
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis is strictly genetic and has nothing to do with microbial transfer
options.D: Men cannot carry the anaerobic bacteria that cause this specific condition

explanation: Because bacterial vaginosis is an internal shift in normal vaginal flora rather than a classic sexually transmitted infection, treating the partner does not stop it from coming back. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h6)

question: What serious pregnancy complication is strongly linked to untreated bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Complete cessation of fetal growth throughout the third trimester
options.B: Severe maternal hypertension and sudden eclamptic fits
options.C: Complete placental detachment during the first trimester
options.D: Preterm labor and premature rupture of membranes

explanation: Enzymes produced by bad bacteria can weaken the bag of waters and trigger early contractions, which can lead to preterm birth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h7)

question: What condition can a newborn baby get after passing through a birth canal affected by a maternal yeast infection?

options.A: Oral thrush
options.B: Neonatal tetanus
options.C: Congenital malaria
options.D: Jaundice

explanation: Babies can pick up Candida yeast during a vaginal birth, which often shows up as white patches inside their mouth called oral thrush. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h7)

question: What type of underwear fabric is best to help prevent recurring vaginal infections?

options.A: Nylon
options.B: Rayon
options.C: Polyester
options.D: Cotton

explanation: Cotton breathes well and absorbs moisture, helping prevent the warm, damp conditions where yeast and anaerobic bacteria love to grow. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which of these practices should a midwife actively advise women against during vaginal hygiene counseling?

options.A: Washing the external vulva gently with clean water and mild soap
options.B: Drying the external genital area thoroughly after taking a bath
options.C: Using antiseptics or soapy water to douche inside the vagina
options.D: Promptly changing menstrual pads every few hours during flow

explanation: Internal douching washes away protective bacteria and changes the pH, making the vagina much more vulnerable to infections. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h8)

question: Why do midwives often use syndromic management instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: Syndromic treatment is always more accurate than laboratory microscopy
options.B: Laboratory tests are expensive and unnecessary for all patients
options.C: Immediate treatment prevents loss to follow-up and treats the patient on the first visit
options.D: National guidelines strictly forbid the use of laboratory tests for reproductive infections

explanation: Many patients do not return for their lab results. Treating them right away ensures they receive the necessary care during their visit. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why does a single syndromic treatment protocol often include a combination of different drugs?

options.A: To cover multiple common pathogens responsible for the same symptom group
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of buying medications separately
options.C: To make the treatment last longer in the patient's bloodstream
options.D: To counteract the strong side effects of the primary antibiotic

explanation: Without lab tests, the treatment protocol covers the most likely organisms that could cause that specific symptom group. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which clinical condition is primarily associated with the lower abdominal pain syndrome algorithm?

options.A: Primary stage genital herpes
options.B: Asymptomatic urinary tract infection
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Simple uncomplicated yeast infection

explanation: Lower abdominal pain in syndromic guidelines points toward pelvic inflammatory disease, which requires treatment for infections like gonorrhea and chlamydia. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h2)

question: A patient presents with a painless genital ulcer during an antenatal visit. Which condition should the midwife suspect using the syndromic flowchart?

options.A: Bacterial vaginosis
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Candidiasis
options.D: Syphilis

explanation: Painless genital ulcers are a key clinical indicator for primary syphilis in the genital ulcer disease algorithm. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the main risk if a midwife treats only the patient and ignores their sexual partners?

options.A: Immediate resistance to all oral antibiotics
options.B: Severe allergic reactions during future pregnancies
options.C: Permanent infertility in the male partner only
options.D: Rapid reinfection of the index patient

explanation: If sexual partners keep the infection without treatment, they can pass it back to the patient soon after sexual activity resumes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard method used to manage sexual partners in syndromic protocols?

options.A: Providing presumptive treatment packs through the index client
options.B: Direct clinical evaluation and treatment at the health facility
options.C: Giving the patient a confidential partner notification slip
options.D: Reporting the infected partner to local law enforcement

explanation: Partner management relies on voluntary notification, confidentiality, and treatment, rather than police involvement or legal force. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why do patients often stop taking their prescribed antibiotics halfway through the dose?

options.A: Their physical symptoms have already disappeared
options.B: National guidelines recommend a three-day maximum
options.C: Healthcare workers advise stopping after symptom relief
options.D: The tablets are too large to swallow comfortably

explanation: Patients often think feeling better means the infection is gone, leading them to stop medication before finishing the full course. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h4)

question: What advice should a midwife give regarding sexual activity during STI treatment?

options.A: Abstain from sexual intercourse until treatment is complete and symptoms clear
options.B: Stop sexual activity only if the male partner develops symptoms
options.C: Limit intercourse to once per week while taking oral medications
options.D: Continue regular sexual activity if using traditional herbal washes

explanation: Continuing sexual intercourse during treatment can spread the infection and lead to immediate reinfection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is a major challenge for syndromic management in many primary healthcare clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory international travel for all infected patients
options.B: Frequent stockouts of essential syndromic medications
options.C: An oversupply of trained midwifery personnel in rural areas
options.D: Excessive availability of advanced laboratory testing equipment

explanation: Drug stockouts and poor supply chains disrupt treatment protocols because the required medications are sometimes unavailable on the shelf. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h5)

question: A patient cannot afford the complete drug regimen prescribed through the syndromic algorithm. What is a practical first step for the midwife?

options.A: Ignore the syndromic guidelines and offer traditional herbs instead
options.B: Explore facility drug revolving funds or assist with subsidized alternatives
options.C: Prescribe only half the dosage to cut the cost in half
options.D: Send the patient away until they can save enough money for private care

explanation: Using facility funds, social welfare support, or subsidized options helps ensure the patient receives the full and correct treatment course. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T10#BMP310_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which strains of HPV are most commonly linked to cervical cancer?

options.A: HPV types 6 and 11
options.B: HPV types 30 and 32
options.C: HPV types 50 and 52
options.D: HPV types 16 and 18

explanation: Strains 16 and 18 are high-risk types responsible for the majority of cervical cancers worldwide. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h1)

question: What usually happens to an HPV infection in the body after a year or two?

options.A: It is cleared naturally by the immune system
options.B: It lies dormant forever without any cellular changes
options.C: It transforms permanently into benign genital warts
options.D: It immediately develops into invasive cervical cancer

explanation: A healthy immune system typically fights off and clears most HPV infections without causing lasting harm. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h1)

question: Who is the primary target group recommended to receive the HPV vaccine?

options.A: Elderly women post-menopause
options.B: Infants under one year old
options.C: Women aged 35 to 45 years
options.D: Girls aged 9 to 14 years

explanation: Vaccinating young adolescent girls before sexual debut provides maximum protection before potential exposure to the virus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why is the HPV vaccine considered a form of primary prevention?

options.A: It treats active genital warts caused by low-risk viral strains
options.B: It prevents the initial acquisition of the virus before infection occurs
options.C: It cures existing cervical cancer cells within a few weeks of treatment
options.D: It replaces the need for any future routine cervical cancer screening

explanation: Primary prevention stops a condition from happening in the first place by building immunity against the virus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which screening method is most widely used and practical for primary health care settings in Nigeria?

options.A: Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)
options.B: Expensive liquid-based cytology tests
options.C: Routine pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Prophylactic radical surgical excision

explanation: VIA is affordable, needs minimal equipment, and gives immediate results, making it ideal for primary clinics. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of a 'screen-and-treat' VIA protocol in remote rural communities?

options.A: It guarantees that she will never contract a viral infection again
options.B: It prevents patient loss to follow-up by treating immediately
options.C: It proves definitively that she already has invasive malignant cancer
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any physical pelvic examination

explanation: Many women in rural areas find it hard to return for follow-up visits, so treating precancerous changes during the same visit saves lives. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which part of the cervix must be sampled during a Pap smear to get an adequate cell specimen?

options.A: The fundus of the uterus
options.B: The lower vaginal wall
options.C: The transformation zone
options.D: The peritoneal cavity

explanation: The transformation zone is where most cervical changes start, making it the key target for cell collection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h4)

question: What does an LSIL result typically mean on a lab report?

options.A: Large spreading invasive malignant tumor of the uterus
options.B: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion with mild dysplasia
options.C: Complete absence of any epithelial cells on the slide
options.D: Normal tissue with zero inflammation or cellular changes

explanation: LSIL stands for low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, which shows mild, often temporary cell changes from HPV. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h4)

question: What color do abnormal precancerous cells turn when exposed to acetic acid during a VIA exam?

options.A: Deep royal blue
options.B: Dark jet black
options.C: Bright neon yellow
options.D: Distinct acetowhite

explanation: Acetic acid causes proteins in abnormal cells to turn a noticeable whitish color against the pink cervix. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of using VIA for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: It is subjective and depends heavily on the provider's visual judgment
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory machinery to analyze the tissue samples
options.C: It causes permanent chemical burns on the healthy parts of the cervix
options.D: It takes at least two weeks for the vinegar reaction results to appear

explanation: Because VIA relies on the naked eye rather than automated lab tests, the provider's skill level affects its accuracy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why is pre-test counseling important before performing a cervical screening test?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will never test positive for an infection
options.B: It chemically alters the cervical cells to make them easier to stain
options.C: It reduces patient anxiety and addresses misconceptions about the procedure
options.D: It completely replaces the need to perform a physical pelvic exam

explanation: Good counseling prepares the client emotionally, explains what to expect, and encourages participation in screening. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h6)

question: A client has a screening result showing a suspicious, advanced cervical lesion. What is the most appropriate next step for the midwife?

options.A: Reassure her that no medical follow-up is ever needed for abnormal results
options.B: Discharge the client and advise her to return in five years for a repeat test
options.C: Administer a dose of routine childhood HPV vaccine to cure the lesion
options.D: Refer the client urgently to a gynecologist for colposcopy and biopsy

explanation: Suspicious or advanced lesions need immediate specialist evaluation and tissue testing to confirm diagnosis and plan care. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h6)

question: What is an iatrogenic reproductive tract infection?

options.A: It only affects women who have never been pregnant before.
options.B: It cannot be treated with standard antibiotic regimens.
options.C: It is exclusively transmitted through sexual intercourse.
options.D: It is acquired during a medical or surgical procedure.

explanation: The term iatrogenic means an illness or infection caused by medical examination or treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must midwives tell the difference between iatrogenic infections and standard sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: They always present with much milder symptoms than other infections.
options.B: They do not involve bacteria or other microbial pathogens.
options.C: They arise from healthcare interventions rather than sexual exposure.
options.D: They resolve completely without the need for medical intervention.

explanation: Identifying the healthcare-related origin helps target infection control practices in the clinic. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of these procedures involves placing a foreign body directly into the uterus?

options.A: Bimanual pelvic examination
options.B: Visual inspection with acetic acid
options.C: Intrauterine device insertion
options.D: Routine external abdominal palpation

explanation: Placing an IUD requires passing the device through the cervix into the uterus, creating a potential pathway for infection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient develops a pelvic infection two days after manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Community-acquired viral exanthem from casual contact
options.B: Iatrogenic infection related to uterine instrumentation
options.C: Congenital infection passed down from the mother
options.D: Spontaneous hormonal infection unrelated to the procedure

explanation: Procedures that cross the cervical barrier into the uterus frequently introduce bacteria, leading to iatrogenic complications. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h2)

question: What natural barrier helps protect the upper reproductive tract from invading bacteria?

options.A: The continuous flow of gastric acid
options.B: The alkaline pH of the vulva
options.C: The outer layer of kidney tissue
options.D: The cervical mucus plug

explanation: Thick cervical mucus acts as a physical block against the upward migration of vaginal microorganisms. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do lower genital tract bacteria typically reach the upper uterus during a medical procedure?

options.A: They travel exclusively through the bloodstream from the lungs.
options.B: They are pulled downward from the fallopian tubes by gravity.
options.C: They multiply rapidly because the procedure removes all white blood cells.
options.D: They are carried upward on instruments passing through the cervix.

explanation: Surgical instruments can inadvertently push resident flora from the vagina and cervix past the internal os into the sterile uterus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is a common sign of an iatrogenic reproductive tract infection following surgery?

options.A: Complete numbness of the lower extremities
options.B: Persistent fever and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the sclera
options.D: Sudden and permanent cessation of breathing

explanation: Infections in the reproductive organs typically trigger an inflammatory fever response along with local pain in the pelvis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why can diagnosing an iatrogenic reproductive tract infection sometimes be tricky?

options.A: Patients never experience any physical pain during these infections.
options.B: Early symptoms can be mistaken for normal post-procedure discomfort.
options.C: Infections only appear years after the procedure has taken place.
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely useless for detecting pelvic bacteria.

explanation: Because some cramping and discomfort are expected after pelvic surgery, abnormal signs are sometimes dismissed until the infection worsens. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which practice is most effective in preventing germs from entering during a pelvic procedure?

options.A: Avoiding the use of gloves to maintain better dexterity
options.B: Administering strong cough medicine before the procedure
options.C: Strict adherence to aseptic technique and hand hygiene
options.D: Keeping the examination room at a very cold temperature

explanation: Hand hygiene and sterile technique stop microorganisms from being transferred from hands or equipment into the patient. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is cleaning the vulva and vagina before a procedure important?

options.A: It permanently alters the hormonal balance of the reproductive tract.
options.B: It completely replaces the need for sterile surgical instruments.
options.C: It acts as a strong pain reliever for the upcoming surgery.
options.D: It reduces the number of bacteria present before instruments enter.

explanation: Lowering the initial microbial load means fewer germs are available to be pushed upward during instrumentation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary medical treatment for a confirmed iatrogenic reproductive tract infection?

options.A: High doses of intravenous water and vitamins
options.B: Complete bed rest without any medication
options.C: Immediate surgical removal of the ovaries
options.D: Appropriate broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy

explanation: Bacterial infections within the reproductive tract require targeted antimicrobial drugs to clear the pathogens. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h6)

question: A midwife notices that a clinic frequently prescribes powerful antibiotics for mild post-procedure discomfort without signs of infection. Which principle of care is being violated?

options.A: Routine surgical asepsis
options.B: Emergency triage ranking
options.C: Antibiotic stewardship
options.D: Informed consent protocols

explanation: Antibiotic stewardship encourages careful and responsible prescribing to avoid creating resistant bacterial strains. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h6)

question: How are most sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections mainly spread?

options.A: Sharing contaminated eating utensils
options.B: Consuming untreated drinking water
options.C: Sexual contact with an infected partner
options.D: Inadequate personal hygiene habits

explanation: These infections are acquired primarily through sexual intercourse or intimate sexual contact. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is catching lower reproductive tract infections early so important for midwives?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any subsequent laboratory testing
options.B: It immediately restores normal hormonal balance in the ovaries
options.C: It prevents the infection from spreading upward into the uterus and tubes
options.D: It guarantees complete immunity against future bacterial exposures

explanation: Prompt treatment stops pathogens from ascending into the upper reproductive organs where they cause severe damage. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h1)

question: What term describes passing an infection from a mother to her baby during pregnancy or childbirth?

options.A: Latent infection
options.B: Vertical transmission
options.C: Horizontal spread
options.D: Secondary invasion

explanation: Vertical transmission specifically refers to the passage of pathogens from mother to child during the perinatal period. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are adolescent girls biologically more vulnerable to certain sexually transmitted infections than older women?

options.A: Their pelvic bones are shaped differently during puberty
options.B: Their immune systems completely ignore bacterial invaders
options.C: They produce lower amounts of protective vaginal flora
options.D: Their cervical cells are more exposed and immature

explanation: Ectocervical maturation changes over time, leaving younger females with vulnerable tissue prone to pathogen penetration. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which organism typically causes a frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge with severe itching?

options.A: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.C: Treponema pallidum
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Trichomoniasis is a parasitic infection classically characterized by a frothy, yellow-green discharge and irritation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h3)

question: What makes Chlamydia trachomatis particularly challenging to manage in routine clinic visits?

options.A: It frequently causes no noticeable symptoms at all
options.B: It resists all known classes of oral antibiotics
options.C: It only affects women who have given birth before
options.D: It changes the physical color of the cervix permanently

explanation: Chlamydia is notorious for being a silent infection, meaning many infected women remain unaware until complications arise. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is syndromic management mainly based on when laboratory tests are not available?

options.A: The patient's family medical history
options.B: Ultrasound imaging of the placenta
options.C: Blood pressure and weight fluctuations
options.D: Observed signs and reported symptoms

explanation: Syndromic management uses clinical algorithms matching visible signs and symptoms to provide immediate treatment during the visit. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why are routine screening checks done during the first antenatal visit?

options.A: To determine the precise date when labor contractions will start
options.B: To measure the baseline hormonal levels of the expectant mother
options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age of the developing fetus
options.D: To detect asymptomatic infections before they harm the pregnancy

explanation: Screening catches hidden infections early, preventing vertical transmission and adverse pregnancy outcomes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h4)

question: What condition can a newborn get during vaginal delivery if the mother has an untreated gonococcal or chlamydial infection?

options.A: Congenital heart defect
options.B: Ophthalmia neonatorum
options.C: Neural tube defect
options.D: Infant respiratory distress

explanation: Babies passing through an infected birth canal often develop eye infections known as ophthalmia neonatorum. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h5)

question: A postpartum woman develops severe lower abdominal pain and foul-smelling lochia a few days after delivery. What prior condition could have contributed significantly to this?

options.A: An untreated lower reproductive tract infection
options.B: Consuming too much spicy food during pregnancy
options.C: Failing to walk around early enough after birth
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding without supplement water

explanation: Pathogens present in the reproductive tract can easily ascend into the uterine cavity after birth, leading to postpartum endometritis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is treating only the female patient not enough when managing sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections?

options.A: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn baby
options.B: It leaves the sexual partner untreated, causing reinfection
options.C: It stops the ovaries from producing normal progesterone
options.D: It permanently ruins the effectiveness of future antibiotics

explanation: Without treating partners, the woman faces almost guaranteed reinfection once sexual activity resumes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of partner notification slips given to patients in the clinic?

options.A: To prove to the midwife that the patient is married
options.B: To track the exact home address of every community member
options.C: To encourage exposed partners to seek testing and treatment
options.D: To serve as a legal permit for receiving free medication

explanation: Notification slips discreetly invite partners to the clinic so they can receive necessary evaluation and therapy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h6)
