question: What is a core way to prevent sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections?

options.A: Underwriting private health insurance
options.B: Consistent and correct barrier method use
options.C: Taking daily multivitamin supplements
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise during pregnancy

explanation: Condoms provide a physical barrier that significantly reduces the transmission of pathogens during intercourse. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must midwives keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health counseling sessions?

options.A: To encourage patients to share accurate information without fear of stigma
options.B: To ensure the hospital meets international accreditation standards
options.C: To guarantee that laboratory test results come out much faster
options.D: To prevent the midwife from feeling stressed during working hours

explanation: A welcoming, stigma-free environment builds trust, making patients more honest about their symptoms and sexual history. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h7)

question: What type of organism causes gonorrhea?

options.A: A Gram-negative diplococcus
options.B: A double-stranded DNA virus
options.C: A Gram-positive spirochete
options.D: A flagellated protozoan parasite

explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a Gram-negative diplococcus bacterium that infects mucosal membranes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h1)

question: How does a baby usually contract gonorrhea from an infected mother?

options.A: Through breastmilk feeding after delivery
options.B: Via airborne droplets in the nursery ward
options.C: Across the placenta during early pregnancy
options.D: During passage through the birth canal

explanation: The infant is exposed to the bacteria directly when passing through an infected maternal cervix and vagina during delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which symptom is most typical of gonococcal cervicitis in women?

options.A: Hard painless ulcer on the vulva
options.B: Lower abdominal rash with small fluid blisters
options.C: Intense itching with thick white cheese discharge
options.D: Purulent yellowish vaginal discharge

explanation: Gonococcal infection causes localized inflammation with a characteristic pus-filled cervical discharge. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant woman tests positive for gonorrhea during routine booking but reports no physical discomfort. What does this clinical picture suggest?

options.A: The laboratory result is a false positive due to normal pregnancy flora.
options.B: She only needs partner notification without taking any antibiotics.
options.C: She has an asymptomatic infection that still requires full treatment.
options.D: Her immune system has successfully cleared the bacteria naturally.

explanation: Many women harbor the infection without symptoms, but treatment is vital to prevent severe pregnancy and neonatal complications. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which laboratory method is widely used as a primary diagnostic tool to identify Neisseria gonorrhoeae from an endocervical swab?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Complete blood count test
options.C: Gram stain microscopy
options.D: Urinalysis reagent strip

explanation: A Gram stain allows the midwife or lab technician to visualize the characteristic Gram-negative diplococci under a microscope. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is routine antenatal screening for sexually transmitted infections recommended during the first booking visit?

options.A: To check if the placenta is attached low in the uterine cavity
options.B: To detect hidden infections early and prevent ascending complications
options.C: To confirm the mother's blood group and rhesus compatibility
options.D: To measure the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: Early detection allows prompt treatment before the infection can ascend to the upper reproductive tract and harm the pregnancy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary antibiotic combination recommended for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea?

options.A: Penicillin and metronidazole
options.B: Ceftriaxone and azithromycin
options.C: Erythromycin and tetracycline
options.D: Amoxicillin and gentamycin

explanation: Standard protocols combine an injectable cephalosporin with an oral macrolide to ensure effective clearance and cover chlamydial coinfection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h4)

question: A woman receives treatment for gonorrhea at the antenatal clinic. What crucial step must the midwife take regarding her partner?

options.A: Refer the partner exclusively to a general surgical outpatient clinic.
options.B: Advise the partner to wait for severe symptoms to appear.
options.C: Treat the partner simultaneously to prevent reinfection.
options.D: Tell the partner to use condoms without needing any medication.

explanation: Simultaneous partner treatment is essential to eliminate the reservoir of infection and prevent the woman from being infected again. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the name of the severe eye infection a newborn can contract from an infected birth canal?

options.A: Purulent keratitis
options.B: Congenital cataract
options.C: Neonatal retinopathy
options.D: Ophthalmia neonatorum

explanation: Ophthalmia neonatorum is a severe form of conjunctivitis acquired by the newborn during passage through a birth canal infected with gonorrhea or chlamydia. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which maternal complication is directly linked to ascending gonococcal infection in the reproductive tract?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Postpartum thyroiditis
options.D: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

explanation: When bacteria ascend from the cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes, it results in Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is partner notification considered a key component of gonorrhea management?

options.A: It breaks the transmission chain by treating hidden reservoirs of infection.
options.B: It proves whether the pregnant woman was faithful to her partner.
options.C: It allows the hospital to collect extra consultation fees from families.
options.D: It serves as a legal punishment for individuals who break marital vows.

explanation: Treating all exposed sexual partners stops ongoing transmission and protects the index patient from getting reinfected. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h6)

question: A patient is afraid to tell her husband about her gonorrhea diagnosis because she fears abandonment. What is the most appropriate initial midwifery action?

options.A: Refuse to treat her until she brings her husband to the clinic forcefully.
options.B: Provide confidential counseling and offer assisted partner notification support.
options.C: Report her case immediately to the local community leaders without consent.
options.D: Tell her to hide the diagnosis and take the medications secretly.

explanation: Empathetic counseling helps address her fears while finding a safe, confidential way to ensure her partner receives treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h6)

question: What kind of germ causes chlamydia?

options.A: An intracellular bacterium
options.B: A double-stranded virus
options.C: A spore-forming fungus
options.D: A multi-celled parasite

explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is a bacterium that must live and multiply inside living host cells to survive. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is the elementary body phase important for the chlamydia bacterium?

options.A: It prevents white blood cells from destroying the pathogen in the blood.
options.B: It provides the primary energy source needed for rapid cell division.
options.C: It neutralizes the acidic pH found inside the human reproductive tract.
options.D: It allows the organism to survive outside host cells and spread infection.

explanation: The elementary body is the tough, infectious form specially adapted to survive outside a host cell long enough to infect a new person. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h1)

question: How is chlamydia most commonly spread between adults?

options.A: Direct airborne droplet spread
options.B: Sharing contaminated clothing
options.C: Unprotected sexual contact
options.D: Drinking from public cups

explanation: Chlamydia spreads primarily through sexual fluids exchanged during unprotected vaginal, anal, or oral sex. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h2)

question: An antenatal client asks how her newborn baby could catch chlamydia during birth. What is the correct answer?

options.A: The baby can pick up the infection while passing through the birth canal.
options.B: The bacteria can cross the placental barrier directly during the third trimester.
options.C: Breast milk from an infected mother carries the active chlamydial organism.
options.D: Airborne transmission in the delivery room exposes the newborn's lungs.

explanation: Neonatal exposure happens vertically when the baby moves through an infected cervix and vagina during delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is chlamydia often called a silent infection?

options.A: Infected individuals lose the ability to speak clearly.
options.B: It causes complete and permanent painless hearing loss.
options.C: The bacteria destroy vocal cords in advanced stages.
options.D: Most infected people do not show any visible symptoms.

explanation: The vast majority of infected men and women experience no symptoms at all, which allows the infection to spread silently. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which symptom is common in female patients with a chlamydia cervical infection?

options.A: Painless white tongue patches
options.B: Mucopurulent vaginal discharge
options.C: Sudden complete hair loss
options.D: Severe itchy skin rashes

explanation: Infection of the cervix causes inflammation that leads to an abnormal yellow or cloudy discharge. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the standard laboratory test used to diagnose chlamydia?

options.A: Nucleic Acid Amplification Testing
options.B: Simple urine dipstick chemical strip
options.C: Microscopic wet mount preparation
options.D: Routine complete blood cell count

explanation: NAAT is the most sensitive and reliable test because it detects the genetic material of the bacteria. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h4)

question: In a clinic without advanced laboratory equipment, which tool is most practical for screening chlamydia?

options.A: Cervical tissue biopsy
options.B: Intravenous contrast X-rays
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Rapid diagnostic test kits

explanation: Rapid tests provide quick, bedside results where complex laboratory equipment is unavailable, helping guide initial care. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which antibiotic must be avoided when treating chlamydia in a pregnant woman?

options.A: Amoxicillin
options.B: Erythromycin
options.C: Doxycycline
options.D: Azithromycin

explanation: Doxycycline is a tetracycline antibiotic that affects fetal bone and tooth development, making it unsafe during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated along with the patient for chlamydia?

options.A: It prevents the bacteria from mutating into a virus.
options.B: It strengthens the patient's long-term immunity.
options.C: It cures the primary patient's chronic headaches.
options.D: It stops the cycle of reinfection between partners.

explanation: If sexual partners are not treated at the same time, they will continuously pass the infection back and forth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h5)

question: What common newborn eye condition is caused by untreated chlamydia during birth?

options.A: Neural tube defects
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Ophthalmia neonatorum

explanation: Babies passing through an infected birth canal frequently develop chlamydial eye infections known as neonatal conjunctivitis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h6)

question: How does untreated chlamydia threaten an ongoing pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the production of normal amniotic fluid entirely
options.B: By blocking the absorption of dietary iron in the placenta
options.C: By increasing the risk of preterm labor and membrane rupture
options.D: By causing permanent high blood pressure in the mother's brain

explanation: Lower genital tract inflammation weakens fetal membranes and stimulates uterine contractions, leading to premature delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent chlamydia?

options.A: Consistent and correct condom use
options.B: Taking daily high-dose vitamin supplements
options.C: Prompt treatment of infected partners
options.D: Regular screening of sexually active groups

explanation: Vitamins do not prevent bacterial transmission; barrier methods and screening are required to stop the spread of chlamydia. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is a major long-term risk of untreated chlamydia infections in women?

options.A: Primary essential hypertension
options.B: Chronic bone density loss
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Tubal factor infertility

explanation: Repeated or untreated upper reproductive tract infections cause scarring and blockage in the fallopian tubes, leading to infertility. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which specific organism causes syphilis?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Treponema pallidum
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation: Syphilis is caused by a spiral-shaped bacterium known as Treponema pallidum. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does the syphilis bacterium typically reach the developing baby during pregnancy?

options.A: It crosses directly through the placenta into fetal circulation
options.B: It ascends from the vagina only during active labor
options.C: It is transmitted exclusively through breast milk after birth
options.D: It enters the amniotic fluid through abdominal wall pores

explanation: The bacteria cross the placental barrier and enter the fetal bloodstream, causing a congenital infection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main sign of early primary syphilis?

options.A: A widespread itchy rash on the trunk
options.B: A thick yellow foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Painful fluid-filled blisters on the vulva
options.D: A painless sore called a chancre

explanation: The hallmark of primary syphilis is the chancre, which is typically a single, firm, and painless ulcer. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which body areas are typically affected by the rash seen in secondary syphilis?

options.A: The inside of the oral cavity exclusively
options.B: Only the abdomen and the lower back
options.C: The scalp and behind the human ears
options.D: Palms of the hands and soles of the feet

explanation: Secondary syphilis frequently produces a distinctive rash that prominently features the palms and soles. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is untreated syphilis in pregnancy dangerous to the unborn baby?

options.A: It stops the fetal lungs from producing surfactant before term delivery
options.B: It causes the placenta to detach completely during the first trimester
options.C: It frequently results in stillbirth, miscarriage, or severe birth defects
options.D: It prevents the mother from producing enough amniotic fluid for growth

explanation: Passing the infection through the placenta often leads to tragic pregnancy losses or severely compromised infants. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is a classic late sign of congenital syphilis in a growing child?

options.A: Asthma and chronic cough
options.B: Hutchinson's teeth
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Enlarged thyroid gland

explanation: Notched, peg-shaped central incisors known as Hutchinson's teeth are a classic late sign of untreated congenital syphilis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary role of nontreponemal tests like VDRL in clinical care?

options.A: Detecting active viral load changes in the bloodstream
options.B: Measuring exact bacterial cell counts under a microscope
options.C: Screening for infection and monitoring response to treatment
options.D: Confirming lifelong immunity after natural infection recovery

explanation: Nontreponemal tests rise and fall with disease activity, making them useful for screening and checking if treatment worked. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h4)

question: What happens to a patient's treponemal test result after they are successfully cured of syphilis?

options.A: It usually remains positive for the rest of their life
options.B: It disappears completely once the skin lesions heal
options.C: It turns negative within two weeks of receiving treatment
options.D: It fluctuates depending on future pregnancies and stress

explanation: Once a person has had syphilis, treponemal antibodies generally persist for life, even after a complete cure. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which medication is the standard treatment for syphilis during pregnancy?

options.A: Benzathine penicillin G
options.B: Erythromycin base
options.C: Ceftriaxone injection
options.D: Metronidazole tablets

explanation: Benzathine penicillin G is the recommended antibiotic that effectively treats the pregnant woman and crosses the placenta to cure the fetus. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why are antibiotics like doxycycline avoided when treating syphilis in pregnancy?

options.A: They neutralize the normal flora of the maternal gastrointestinal tract
options.B: They cause abnormal bone growth and tooth discoloration in the fetus
options.C: They provoke severe allergic reactions in almost every pregnant woman
options.D: They fail to cross the placental barrier in high enough concentrations

explanation: Tetracyclines inhibit bone growth and stain developing teeth in utero, making them unsafe during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h5)

question: A pregnant woman is treated for early syphilis at her clinic. What essential extra step must the midwife take to prevent reinfection?

options.A: Prescribe prophylactic antibiotics for the baby after delivery
options.B: Perform monthly ultrasound scans to check fetal limb length
options.C: Isolate the woman from her family until breastfeeding ends
options.D: Trace, test, and treat her sexual partner concurrently

explanation: Treating sexual partners is necessary to stop the cycle of reinfection and protect both mother and baby. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard goal of follow-up care after maternal syphilis treatment?

options.A: Confirming absence of reinfection before the expected date of delivery
options.B: Monitoring decreasing nontreponemal antibody titers over time
options.C: Permanently removing treponemal antibodies from blood tests
options.D: Ensuring the sexual partner has received proper curative therapy

explanation: Treponemal antibodies usually remain positive for life regardless of successful treatment, so making them negative is not a clinical goal. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h6)

question: What type of organism causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: A protozoan parasite
options.B: A gram-negative bacterium
options.C: A double-stranded virus
options.D: A superficial fungus

explanation: Trichomonas vaginalis is a single-celled protozoan that uses flagella to move through genital fluids. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h1)

question: Name the primary method by which Trichomonas vaginalis spreads from person to person.

options.A: Insect bites from mosquitoes
options.B: Sharing contaminated bath towels
options.C: Unprotected vaginal intercourse
options.D: Consuming unclean well water

explanation: The parasite relies on direct genital-to-genital contact during sexual activity to survive and infect a new host. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following is a classic clinical sign sometimes seen on the cervix during a speculum examination of a woman with trichomoniasis?

options.A: Hard, painless ulcerative chancre
options.B: Clear fluid-filled vesicular clusters
options.C: A thick, white, curd-like plaque layer
options.D: Strawberry cervix with punctate hemorrhages

explanation: Tiny red spots called punctate hemorrhages give the cervix a strawberry-like appearance due to capillary dilation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h2)

question: A woman comes to the antenatal clinic complaining of a foul-smelling, yellow-green vaginal discharge and severe vulvar itching. Which infection should the midwife strongly suspect first?

options.A: Normal leukorrhea
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Uncomplicated UTI
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: A frothy yellow-green discharge with itching is a hallmark presentation of trichomoniasis in women. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the traditional bedside or clinic-level test where a midwife mixes vaginal discharge with saline to look for moving parasites under a microscope?

options.A: Urinalysis reagent strip
options.B: Wet mount microscopy
options.C: Full blood count analysis
options.D: Rapid plasma reagin test

explanation: A wet mount allows the midwife to quickly look for actively swimming trichomonads in a fresh saline preparation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why do healthcare providers prefer Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs) when they are available?

options.A: They provide superior sensitivity and accuracy
options.B: They eliminate the need for any physical exam
options.C: They yield results within five minutes
options.D: They require no electricity or equipment

explanation: NAATs detect even tiny amounts of parasite genetic material, making them much more reliable than simple microscope checks. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which group of medications serves as the primary treatment for trichomoniasis?

options.A: First-generation cephalosporins
options.B: Nitroimidazoles like metronidazole
options.C: Topical antifungal azoles
options.D: Broad-spectrum penicillins

explanation: Drugs in the nitroimidazole class, such as metronidazole and tinidazole, are uniquely effective against anaerobic protozoa like Trichomonas. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h4)

question: What critical warning must a midwife give a client prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis?

options.A: Take the medication exclusively on an empty stomach
options.B: Stop taking the tablets immediately if urine turns dark
options.C: Avoid drinking any alcohol during the treatment period
options.D: Apply the oral pills directly into the vaginal canal

explanation: Mixing metronidazole with alcohol causes unpleasant systemic side effects like severe nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is a well-documented pregnancy complication linked to untreated trichomoniasis?

options.A: Preterm delivery and low birth weight
options.B: Congenital skeletal malformations
options.C: Primary postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Gestational proteinuric hypertension

explanation: The inflammatory response triggered by the parasite can stimulate uterine contractions and weaken membranes, leading to early delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h5)

question: How does trichomoniasis indirectly increase the vulnerability of a pregnant woman to other viral infections?

options.A: By completely blocking the normal absorption of dietary iron
options.B: By causing localized inflammation and tissue irritation in the genital tract
options.C: By directly suppressing the entire bone marrow stem cell production
options.D: By permanently lowering systemic blood pressure throughout gestation

explanation: Local inflammation brings immune cells to the area and causes micro-abrasions, making it easier for viruses like HIV to enter the body. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why must sexual partners of a patient treated for trichomoniasis also receive treatment?

options.A: To prevent rapid reinfection of the index patient
options.B: To boost the immune system of the male partner
options.C: To cure a co-existing urinary tract infection
options.D: To prevent permanent male sterility

explanation: Treating only one partner leaves the door open for the parasite to be passed right back during their next sexual encounter. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which strategy is NOT recommended when counseling a patient about preventing future episodes of trichomoniasis?

options.A: Relying solely on herbal vaginal douches after intercourse
options.B: Using barrier methods like condoms consistently during sex
options.C: Ensuring sexual partners are treated at the same time
options.D: Seeking prompt medical care if abnormal symptoms return

explanation: Vaginal douching does not cure trichomoniasis and can actually push the infection higher into the reproductive tract or disrupt healthy flora. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the main organism responsible for most cases of vaginal yeast infections?

options.A: Gardnerella vaginalis
options.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.C: Candida albicans
options.D: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation: Candida albicans is a fungus that naturally lives in the body in small amounts and causes yeast infections when it overgrows. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why are vaginal yeast infections generally not classed as classic sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: It only occurs when a patient has a completely destroyed immune system.
options.B: It only affects women who have never engaged in any form of sexual intercourse.
options.C: It cannot be found in male partners under any clinical circumstances.
options.D: It arises mainly from an overgrowth of fungi already present in the normal vaginal flora.

explanation: Yeast infections usually result from an internal imbalance of normal vaginal microbes rather than being strictly passed through sexual contact. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which of these commonly triggers an overgrowth of vaginal yeast by killing off protective bacteria?

options.A: Antihypertensive drugs
options.B: Low dietary protein intake
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Antibiotics kill beneficial bacteria like lactobacilli along with bad bacteria, removing the competition that keeps yeast in check. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h2)

question: How does uncontrolled diabetes make a patient more vulnerable to yeast infections?

options.A: High sugar levels in body fluids provide an excellent food source for fungi to grow.
options.B: Elevated blood glucose completely blocks the body from producing red blood cells.
options.C: Diabetes permanently stops the ovaries from producing any protective progesterone.
options.D: Sugar causes the vaginal walls to become entirely dry and devoid of mucus.

explanation: Fungi feed on glucose, so excess sugar in body tissues and secretions encourages the yeast to multiply rapidly. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h2)

question: What type of vaginal discharge is most commonly linked with a yeast infection?

options.A: Bloody and watery with large clots
options.B: Thick, white, and cottage-cheese-like
options.C: Frothy, yellow-green, and foul-smelling
options.D: Thin, gray, and fishy-smelling

explanation: Typical yeast discharge is thick and white, resembling curdled milk or cottage cheese, without a strong odor. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h3)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with intense vaginal itching and a thick, odorless white discharge. What does this point to?

options.A: Trichomoniasis
options.B: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Gonococcal cervicitis

explanation: Severe itching combined with a thick, odorless white discharge is the classic presentation of a yeast infection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h3)

question: What solution is added to a vaginal wet mount in the lab to dissolve cells and highlight yeast?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide
options.B: 10% potassium hydroxide
options.C: Glacial acetic acid
options.D: Normal saline solution

explanation: Potassium hydroxide dissolves background cells and bacteria, making fungal spores and hyphae clearly visible under the microscope. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the typical range of vaginal pH in a patient with a simple yeast infection?

options.A: Highly alkaline range above 7.5
options.B: Normal acidic range between 4.0 and 4.5
options.C: Neutral range sitting strictly at 7.0
options.D: Exceedingly acidic range below 2.0

explanation: Unlike other vaginal infections that raise the pH, yeast infections generally do not change the normal acidic balance of the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is a common oral medication used to treat uncomplicated yeast infections?

options.A: Azithromycin
options.B: Metronidazole
options.C: Penicillin V
options.D: Fluconazole

explanation: Fluconazole is a widely used oral antifungal drug that often clears yeast infections with a single dose in non-pregnant patients. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why must midwives warn patients using oil-based vaginal antifungal creams about latex barrier methods?

options.A: Latex triggers a severe allergic reaction when mixed with oral antifungal drugs.
options.B: The medication reacts chemically to turn the latex condom completely invisible.
options.C: The oil in the cream can weaken latex and cause condoms to break easily.
options.D: Condoms absorb all the active drug, making the cream totally useless.

explanation: Oil-based creams and pessaries can damage latex integrity, leading to broken condoms and failed contraception. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the preferred treatment for a yeast infection during pregnancy?

options.A: Strong systemic antibiotic therapy with metronidazole
options.B: Intravenous antifungal infusions for three days
options.C: High-dose oral fluconazole taken as a single pill
options.D: Topical azole creams or pessaries for seven days

explanation: Topical treatments are preferred and considered safe during pregnancy, while oral azoles are restricted, especially early on. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why are oral antifungal pills generally avoided in the first trimester of pregnancy?

options.A: The pregnant stomach acid destroys all antifungal tablets before they can dissolve.
options.B: Oral drugs cause immediate and permanent blindness in the developing fetus.
options.C: There are potential safety concerns regarding birth defects with systemic absorption.
options.D: Oral medications are completely incapable of reaching vaginal tissues in pregnant women.

explanation: To protect the developing organs of the fetus during the first trimester, systemic oral antifungals are avoided in favor of safe local treatments. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h6)

question: How do tight synthetic clothes and non-breathable underwear contribute to repeat yeast infections?

options.A: Synthetic fibers release toxic chemicals that directly stimulate fungal spore production.
options.B: They trap heat and moisture in the vulvar area, creating an ideal environment for fungi to multiply.
options.C: They prevent the natural blood supply from reaching the external genitalia.
options.D: They physically scrape the vaginal walls and cause bleeding that attracts fungi.

explanation: Fungi thrive in warm, dark, and humid conditions, which are easily created by tight synthetic garments that block air circulation. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h7)

question: A patient gets a yeast infection every month after using perfumed soaps and internal douches. What advice should the midwife give?

options.A: Apply perfumed deodorant sprays directly inside the vagina to kill the yeast.
options.B: Increase the frequency of douching to twice daily to wash away the fungi.
options.C: Stop douching and using scented soaps, as they destroy the protective vaginal flora.
options.D: Switch from perfumed soaps to strong antiseptic bleaches for washing.

explanation: Douching and harsh chemicals wash away good bacteria and raise the risk of repeated fungal overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which helpful bacteria is normally found in large numbers in a healthy vagina?

options.A: Candida albicans
options.B: Lactobacilli
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: Lactobacilli are the main protective bacteria that keep the vagina at a healthy, acidic level. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h1)

question: What usually happens when the normal acid level in the vagina drops?

options.A: Fungal spores grow faster inside the uterus.
options.B: Normal bacteria are completely destroyed by a drop in body temperature.
options.C: Harmful bacteria multiply quickly when protective lactic acid goes down.
options.D: Lactobacilli need an alkaline environment to make hydrogen peroxide.

explanation: Lactobacilli keep the vaginal environment acidic and safe; when they decrease, harmful bacteria can take over. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which organism forms a stubborn protective layer (biofilm) on vaginal walls during bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Gardnerella vaginalis
options.C: Treponema pallidum
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Gardnerella vaginalis is a main organism in bacterial vaginosis that creates a dense biofilm, making the infection harder to treat. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h2)

question: What causes the strong fishy smell often noticed in bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Acids made by dying protective bacteria
options.B: Secondary fungal fermentation inside the vagina
options.C: Breakdown of excess blood from minor bleeding
options.D: Chemical compounds (amines) produced by overgrowing bad bacteria

explanation: The breakdown of proteins by anaerobic bacteria creates volatile amines, which cause the distinct fishy odor. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which everyday hygiene habit is strongly linked to upsetting the natural vaginal balance?

options.A: Wearing cotton underwear
options.B: Washing the vulva with plain water
options.C: Wiping from front to back
options.D: Vaginal douching

explanation: Douching washes away helpful bacteria and changes the natural pH, which can lead to bacterial overgrowth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h3)

question: A patient at the clinic mentions she routinely washes inside her vagina with medicated soap because of discharge. What is the best advice to give her first?

options.A: Switch from contraceptive pills to an injection.
options.B: Stop washing inside the vagina because it washes away protective bacteria.
options.C: Use a stronger antiseptic liquid to kill remaining germs.
options.D: Take oral antibiotics before every menstrual period.

explanation: Washing inside the vagina removes the natural protective flora, so advising the patient to stop internal washing is essential. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h3)

question: What kind of discharge is typical in bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Bloody and clumpy
options.B: Thin, grayish-white, and smooth
options.C: Thick, white, and cottage-cheese-like
options.D: Frothy, yellow-green, and foul-smelling

explanation: Bacterial vaginosis typically causes a smooth, watery, grayish-white discharge that coats the area evenly. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why does the fishy odor of bacterial vaginosis often get stronger right after sexual intercourse?

options.A: Friction pushes trapped bacteria deeper into the cervix.
options.B: Semen stimulates the rapid growth of fungi.
options.C: Semen is alkaline and reacts with the bacterial compounds to release the smell.
options.D: Intercourse introduces new foreign bacteria.

explanation: The basic pH of semen reacts with the amines present in bacterial vaginosis, making the fishy smell much stronger. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h4)

question: How many of Amsel's signs must be present to diagnose bacterial vaginosis clinically?

options.A: At least two
options.B: At least three
options.C: Only one
options.D: All four

explanation: A reliable clinical diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis requires at least three out of the four Amsel criteria. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h5)

question: What are 'clue cells' when seen under a microscope?

options.A: White blood cells fighting a fungal infection
options.B: Vaginal skin cells covered in clusters of bacteria
options.C: Spores formed by parasites
options.D: Immature cells shed quickly from an inflamed cervix

explanation: Clue cells are epithelial cells whose edges are covered by layers of attached bacteria, giving them a speckled look. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which common oral antibiotic is usually prescribed to treat bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Metronidazole
options.B: Amoxicillin
options.C: Benzylpenicillin
options.D: Ciprofloxacin

explanation: Metronidazole is the primary medication used to treat bacterial vaginosis, taken either as a pill or used topically. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient taking oral metronidazole asks if she can drink a beer with friends this weekend. What is the best response?

options.A: Stop taking the antibiotic early if you want to drink alcohol.
options.B: Drink only small amounts on the last day of treatment.
options.C: Switch to a cream so you can drink alcohol safely.
options.D: Avoid alcohol completely because it causes severe sickness when mixed with this drug.

explanation: Mixing oral metronidazole with alcohol can cause a severe reaction with heavy nausea and vomiting. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which major pregnancy complication is linked to untreated bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Preterm birth
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: High blood pressure in pregnancy

explanation: Bacterial vaginosis is a known risk factor for infections that can trigger early labor and lead to a preterm delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why does bacterial vaginosis increase a woman's chance of getting other infections like HIV?

options.A: The high vaginal pH attracts viruses into the cervix.
options.B: The loss of normal protective flora and irritated tissue lower natural defense barriers.
options.C: The bacteria destroy white blood cells in the bloodstream.
options.D: Metronidazole weakens the immune system.

explanation: Without protective Lactobacilli and with irritated tissue, it is much easier for external viruses and germs to invade. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why should a patient finish all her antibiotics even if her symptoms go away early?

options.A: Stopping early leaves strong bacteria alive, which can bring the infection back.
options.B: Remaining pills are needed for sexual partners.
options.C: Unfinished doses turn into toxic substances in the stomach.
options.D: Unfinished pills expire quickly in storage.

explanation: Completing the full medication ensures all bacteria hidden in the biofilm are cleared out, lowering the chance of a relapse. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h8)

question: A patient returns because her bacterial vaginosis came back two weeks after treatment. What is the best next step for the midwife?

options.A: Scold her for not bringing her partner for treatment.
options.B: Explain that return infections are common and discuss avoiding triggers like douching.
options.C: Tell her to stop using modern family planning methods.
options.D: Tell her that medical treatments do not work.

explanation: Reassuring the patient and talking about simple prevention habits helps manage common infection relapses. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h8)

question: What is the primary definition of amenorrhea?

options.A: The complete absence of menstruation
options.B: Painful cramping during the menstrual cycle
options.C: Bleeding that lasts longer than seven days
options.D: Cycles occurring more frequently than every twenty days

explanation: Amenorrhea describes a situation where a woman or girl does not experience menstrual bleeding when she normally should. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is pregnancy considered a normal reason for amenorrhea?

options.A: Because progesterone levels drop to zero immediately after conception
options.B: Because the ovaries permanently stop producing eggs during gestation
options.C: Because hormonal changes naturally pause the shedding of the uterine lining
options.D: Because the uterus sheds its lining through alternative pathways

explanation: High levels of progesterone and estrogen during pregnancy maintain the endometrium rather than allowing it to break down and bleed. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h1)

question: At what age is primary amenorrhea investigated if secondary sexual characteristics are completely absent?

options.A: Seventeen years
options.B: Thirteen years
options.C: Fifteen years
options.D: Nineteen years

explanation: If a girl reaches age thirteen without starting her period and also shows no signs of breast development or other pubertal changes, primary amenorrhea is investigated. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which genetic condition is a common cause of primary amenorrhea along with short stature and a webbed neck?

options.A: Marfan syndrome
options.B: Down syndrome
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Turner syndrome

explanation: Turner syndrome involves a missing or abnormal X chromosome, causing ovarian failure and primary amenorrhea along with specific physical traits. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h2)

question: How many months of missed periods are usually required to diagnose secondary amenorrhea in a woman with previously irregular cycles?

options.A: One month
options.B: Six months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Twelve months

explanation: For women with irregular baseline cycles, healthcare providers wait for a period of six months without bleeding before making a diagnosis of secondary amenorrhea. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h3)

question: A 22-year-old female marathon runner stops menstruating after drastically increasing her training and losing weight. What has she most likely developed?

options.A: Constitutional delay
options.B: Secondary amenorrhea
options.C: Mullerian agenesis
options.D: Primary amenorrhea

explanation: Since she previously had normal periods and has now lost them due to lifestyle changes and low body weight, she fits the criteria for secondary amenorrhea. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard anatomical area used to classify the causes of amenorrhea?

options.A: Renal compartment
options.B: Hypothalamic compartment
options.C: Outflow tract
options.D: Ovarian compartment

explanation: The kidney system is not one of the four main diagnostic compartments for amenorrhea, whereas outflow, ovarian, pituitary, and hypothalamic systems are. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h4)

question: How does a prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor typically cause secondary amenorrhea?

options.A: By directly destroying the physical structure of the ovaries
options.B: By suppressing the normal release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone from the brain
options.C: By neutralizing estrogen circulating in the bloodstream
options.D: By causing the inner lining of the uterus to shed constantly

explanation: High prolactin levels interfere with the hypothalamic signaling axis, halting the hormonal cascade needed for ovulation and menstruation. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the very first test a midwife should perform when evaluating a patient with amenorrhea?

options.A: Thyroid panel
options.B: Pregnancy test
options.C: Pelvic ultrasound
options.D: Progesterone challenge test

explanation: Pregnancy is the most common cause of missed menses and must always be ruled out first in any reproductive-age female. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h5)

question: What does a positive withdrawal bleed after a progesterone challenge test indicate about the patient's body?

options.A: She has adequate estrogen levels and a functional outflow tract
options.B: Her pituitary gland is producing excessive amounts of prolactin
options.C: Her thyroid gland is severely overactive
options.D: She has complete failure of both ovaries

explanation: If bleeding occurs after giving progesterone, it proves the uterine lining was built up by estrogen and the pathway out is open. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of prescribing cyclic progestins to a patient who does not ovulate regularly?

options.A: To immediately stimulate egg production
options.B: To protect the uterine lining from overgrowth
options.C: To permanently cure hypothalamic disorders
options.D: To lower circulating prolactin levels

explanation: Regular shedding induced by progestins prevents the endometrium from building up unchecked under continuous estrogen, which reduces the risk of cellular changes. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is surgery the appropriate management for a patient diagnosed with Asherman's syndrome?

options.A: Because the ovaries have stopped producing all circulating hormones
options.B: Because the condition involves physical scar tissue blocking the uterine cavity
options.C: Because the pituitary gland has developed a benign tumor
options.D: Because hormonal pills cannot be absorbed by women with this condition

explanation: Asherman's syndrome consists of intrauterine adhesions that require physical removal to restore the normal shape and function of the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h6)

question: How should a midwife best support a patient who is distressed about potential infertility caused by amenorrhea?

options.A: By focusing solely on surgical procedures without discussing her feelings
options.B: By offering empathetic listening and clear education about treatment options
options.C: By assuring her that pregnancy is guaranteed once she gains weight
options.D: By telling her that missing periods is a normal part of modern life

explanation: Holistic care requires acknowledging emotional concerns and providing accurate, reassuring information about how treating the root cause can restore health. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which specialist is most essential to include when managing a patient whose amenorrhea stems from severe restrictive eating habits?

options.A: A physical therapist
options.B: A neonatal pediatrician
options.C: A registered dietitian
options.D: A surgical specialist

explanation: Nutritional rehabilitation is crucial for patients whose amenorrhea is linked to eating disorders or low energy availability, making dietitians key team members. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the main physical cause of a vesicovaginal fistula in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe urinary tract infections
options.B: Congenital pelvic malformations
options.C: Prolonged obstructed labor
options.D: Untreated gestational diabetes

explanation: When labor is blocked for a long time, the baby's head presses hard against the pelvis. This cuts off blood flow and causes the tissue to die, creating an opening. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why does prolonged pressure from the baby's head create a hole between the bladder and vagina?

options.A: It causes an infection that dissolves the bladder wall
options.B: It forces the baby's bones to puncture the internal organs
options.C: It stretches the pelvic floor muscles until they tear open
options.D: It cuts off blood supply and causes tissue death

explanation: When pressure stops blood flow, the tissue lacks oxygen and dies away, leaving an abnormal opening between the organs. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Young maternal age
options.B: Prolonged obstructed labor
options.C: Inadequate dietary calcium
options.D: Accidental surgical trauma

explanation: Not having enough calcium in the diet affects bones, but it does not directly cause the tissue damage that forms a fistula. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why are teenage mothers at a much higher risk of developing a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Their bladder muscles are weaker
options.B: Their pelvic bones are not yet fully grown
options.C: They reject conventional antenatal care
options.D: Their urine is naturally more acidic

explanation: An immature pelvis makes it harder for the baby to pass through, leading to a much higher chance of prolonged obstructed labor. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the main sign that a woman has a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Inability to pass urine at all
options.B: Continuous and uncontrollable urine leakage
options.C: Passing blood clots through the urethra
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain during menstruation

explanation: Because urine completely bypasses the normal control valve, it leaks out through the vagina all the time. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h3)

question: A patient leaks urine after a hard labor, but the hole is too small to see. What test helps confirm the diagnosis?

options.A: The blue dye test
options.B: An abdominal ultrasound scan
options.C: A random blood sugar test
options.D: A complete blood count

explanation: Putting a special blue dye into the bladder helps reveal tiny fistulas when the colored fluid stains a cotton pad in the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is a common social challenge faced by women living with an untreated vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Mandatory relocation to urban centers
options.B: Stigmatization and abandonment by family
options.C: Automatic exemption from local taxes
options.D: Immediate promotion in their local workplace

explanation: Constant leaking and odor often cause people in the community to misunderstand the condition, leading to social rejection and isolation. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is emotional and social support just as important as physical care for a patient with a VVF?

options.A: The condition causes severe emotional trauma and isolation
options.B: Emotional stress prevents the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: Mental health status directly dictates the surgical closure rate
options.D: Hospital policy requires psychiatric clearance before any exam

explanation: Living with constant leakage and social judgment causes deep emotional distress, meaning patients need strong emotional support alongside medical treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care right after a VVF repair surgery?

options.A: Encouraging early ambulation within two hours
options.B: Keeping the urinary bladder continuously drained
options.C: Removing the indwelling catheter by the first morning
options.D: Administering strong laxatives to prevent straining

explanation: Keeping the bladder empty stops urine from building up and putting pressure on the fresh stitches, giving the wound time to heal. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h5)

question: A patient who had a VVF repair yesterday suddenly stops draining urine and feels sharp lower abdominal pain. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Remove the catheter immediately to let her void
options.B: Document the finding and wait for the doctor
options.C: Administer a strong diuretic medication
options.D: Check the tubing for kinks or blockages

explanation: Checking the tube first helps find any simple blockages that are stopping urine from flowing out safely. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is a key part of community reintegration programs for VVF survivors?

options.A: Full exemption from community leadership roles
options.B: Mandatory relocation to a different state
options.C: Vocational training and skills acquisition
options.D: Assignment of permanent government housing

explanation: Learning a practical trade helps survivors earn their own money and rebuild their confidence after overcoming the condition. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h6)

question: How do midwives best help stop the problem of VVF in local communities over the long term?

options.A: Enforcing strict legal penalties against traditional healers
options.B: Performing routine fistula repairs in primary health clinics
options.C: Providing financial grants to families of pregnant women
options.D: Promoting hospital delivery and proper partograph use

explanation: Using partographs to monitor labor and encouraging births in health facilities helps stop prolonged labor before a fistula can form. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: A complete tear of the perineal body reaching the anal sphincter
options.B: A backward displacement of the uterus into the rectal wall
options.C: An infection of the Bartholin gland causing painful swelling
options.D: An abnormal opening between the rectum and the vagina

explanation: A rectovaginal fistula is an abnormal opening or tract that connects the rectum to the mucosal surface of the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is rectovaginal fistula considered a major public health issue in Nigeria?

options.A: It is closely linked to obstructed labor and limited access to emergency care
options.B: It occurs mostly as a rare side effect of routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It develops quickly from untreated viral infections common in urban slums
options.D: It is primarily caused by genetic disorders inherited within specific ethnic groups

explanation: Delays in reaching emergency obstetric care during prolonged labor lead to severe tissue damage and fistula formation in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which factor is responsible for the majority of rectovaginal fistula cases in Nigeria?

options.A: Congenital anatomical defects
options.B: Routine use of episiotomy
options.C: Prolonged obstructed labor
options.D: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head cuts off the blood supply to the tissues between the vagina and rectum, leading to tissue death and fistula formation. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h2)

question: How does tissue ischemia lead to fistula formation during difficult childbirth?

options.A: Compressed blood vessels starve the tissues of oxygen until they die and slough off
options.B: Rapid hormonal shifts cause the vaginal wall to dissolve during hard labor
options.C: Strong uterine contractions physically tear the front wall of the rectum open
options.D: Infected amniotic fluid eats directly through the muscle layers within minutes

explanation: Prolonged pressure compresses local blood vessels, causing ischemia and necrosis that eventually creates a hole between the two organs. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary symptom that leads a woman to seek care for a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Passage of gas or stool through the vagina
options.B: Severe sharp pain during sexual intercourse
options.C: A large painful lump hanging from the vulva
options.D: Inability to control her urine flow

explanation: Because the tract connects the rectum and vagina, intestinal contents pass unnaturally through the vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why do many women with a rectovaginal fistula delay seeking treatment in local communities?

options.A: Traditional herbal remedies always cure the condition without hospital visits
options.B: Government hospitals refuse to admit women with pelvic floor injuries
options.C: They experience severe social stigma and deep personal embarrassment
options.D: They assume the condition will close completely on its own within a year

explanation: The nature of fecal incontinence causes profound psychological distress, leading many women to hide their condition out of shame. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which simple clinical test involves putting colored fluid into the rectum to check for leakage into the vagina?

options.A: Urinary catheter flow rate test
options.B: Complete blood count analysis
options.C: Pap smear cytology screen
options.D: Methylene blue dye test

explanation: Instilling methylene blue into the rectum helps highlight hidden or tiny fistulous tracts by staining a swab placed in the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h4)

question: A patient presents to the clinic with suspected RVF, but visual inspection of the posterior vaginal wall is unclear. What basic bedside evaluation can the midwife perform next?

options.A: An immediate exploratory laparotomy under general anesthesia
options.B: A digital rectal and vaginal examination to feel for the opening
options.C: A barium swallow study to trace the entire gastrointestinal tract
options.D: A full pelvic ultrasound scan using a high-frequency probe

explanation: Palpating the rectovaginal septum between a finger in the rectum and one in the vagina is a reliable bedside method to feel tissue defects. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of postoperative dietary management after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To encourage rapid weight gain through high-protein solid meals
options.B: To prevent dehydration by forcing large amounts of dairy products
options.C: To stimulate immediate bowel evacuation within twelve hours
options.D: To minimize bowel movements and protect the surgical repair site

explanation: Low-residue diets and softeners reduce stool frequency and bulk, preventing undue strain on the newly repaired tissues. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why is keeping an indwelling urinary catheter in place important after fistula surgery?

options.A: It prevents a full bladder from pressing against and straining the repair site
options.B: It keeps the patient completely bedridden to ensure absolute physical rest
options.C: It stops vaginal secretions from contaminating the fresh abdominal incision
options.D: It allows accurate measurement of the patient's daily fluid intake needs

explanation: A distended urinary bladder can exert pressure on the anterior vaginal wall, disrupting delicate sutures placed during the repair. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which strategy is most effective for preventing obstetric rectovaginal fistulas at the community level?

options.A: Encouraging home deliveries attended by experienced traditional birth attendants
options.B: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all pregnant teenagers in the third trimester
options.C: Promoting skilled attendance at birth and prompt referral for obstructed labor
options.D: Providing routine annual pelvic exams for all women of childbearing age

explanation: Preventing prolonged obstructed labor through timely intervention and skilled care stops the tissue necrosis that causes fistulas. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is psychosocial support an essential part of nursing care for a woman recovering from fistula repair?

options.A: She often faces profound emotional trauma, stigma, and social isolation
options.B: Psychological therapy replaces the need for proper postoperative hygiene
options.C: Mental stress directly prevents surgical wounds from receiving blood supply
options.D: Counseling is required by law before any patient can be discharged home

explanation: The chronic leakage and odor cause severe emotional distress and social withdrawal, making psychological healing just as important as physical repair. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h6)

question: Name the primary muscle group that forms the main support of the pelvic floor.

options.A: Rectus abdominis muscle
options.B: Levator ani muscle complex
options.C: Transversus abdominis muscle
options.D: Obturator internus muscle

explanation: The levator ani muscles create a supportive sling at the base of the pelvis that holds the pelvic organs in place. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h1)

question: What happens to the pelvic organs when the uterosacral and cardinal ligaments lose their strength?

options.A: They rotate 180 degrees inside the peritoneal cavity
options.B: They shift laterally toward the pelvic sidewalls
options.C: They are pulled upward toward the diaphragm
options.D: They descend downward into the vaginal canal

explanation: These specific ligaments anchor the upper vagina and uterus; when they weaken, gravity and abdominal pressure cause the uterus to drop. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which of the following is the single greatest risk factor for developing uterine prolapse?

options.A: Multiple vaginal deliveries
options.B: Consuming a high-sodium diet
options.C: A history of cesarean sections
options.D: Regular participation in sports

explanation: Stretching and tearing of pelvic tissues during repeated vaginal births significantly weaken pelvic floor support over time. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h2)

question: A 55-year-old market trader presents with symptoms of uterine prolapse after years of carrying heavy loads on her head. Why does heavy lifting contribute to this condition?

options.A: It prevents normal blood circulation to the pelvic bones
options.B: It chronically increases intra-abdominal pressure downward
options.C: It rapidly depletes systemic estrogen levels in women
options.D: It causes direct trauma to the cervix during movement

explanation: Straining and lifting force intra-abdominal contents downward against a pelvic floor that may already be weakened. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which physical sensation is most commonly reported by women experiencing early uterine prolapse?

options.A: A constant burning sensation during urination
options.B: Sudden numbness in both lower extremities
options.C: A heavy, dragging feeling in the pelvis
options.D: Sharp, stabbing pains in the lower back

explanation: The descent of the uterus pulls on supporting ligaments, creating a characteristic downward dragging or pressure sensation. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h3)

question: Why do symptoms of uterine prolapse generally improve after the patient rests in bed?

options.A: Fluid retention in the lower body stops completely
options.B: Intra-abdominal pressure increases while sleeping
options.C: The pelvic muscles permanently repair themselves overnight
options.D: Gravity no longer pulls the pelvic organs downward

explanation: Horizontal positioning removes the downward gravitational pull on the unsupported uterus, temporarily relieving pressure. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h3)

question: At which grade of uterine prolapse does the cervix descend all the way to the level of the vaginal opening?

options.A: Fourth-degree
options.B: Zero-degree
options.C: Second-degree
options.D: First-degree

explanation: Second-degree prolapse means the cervix has dropped down to the level of the introitus or vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h4)

question: What term is used when the entire uterus protrudes completely outside the vaginal opening?

options.A: Vaginal vault rupture
options.B: Cervical ectropion
options.C: Uterine procidentia
options.D: Adnexal torsion

explanation: Procidentia describes advanced prolapse where the entire uterus has fallen outside the vaginal introitus. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h4)

question: During a pelvic examination for suspected prolapse, why is the patient asked to cough or bear down?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of urine left in the bladder
options.B: To increase intra-abdominal pressure and show maximum descent
options.C: To test the neurological reflexes of the abdominal wall
options.D: To relax the perineal muscles for easier speculum insertion

explanation: Straining or coughing raises intra-abdominal pressure, revealing the true degree of organ prolapse that might not be visible at rest. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which clinical tool is commonly used during the assessment to inspect the vaginal walls and cervix for sores or trauma?

options.A: A pelvic pelvimeter
options.B: A vaginal speculum
options.C: A uterine sound
options.D: A fetal stethoscope

explanation: A speculum allows direct visual inspection of the vaginal tissues to check for friction-induced ulceration or infection. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which non-surgical device can be inserted into the vagina to physically support a prolapsed uterus?

options.A: A hormone ring
options.B: A cervical cap
options.C: An intrauterine device
options.D: A vaginal pessary

explanation: A pessary is a removable silicone or rubber device placed in the vagina to hold the pelvic organs in place. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary goal of conservative nursing management for early uterine prolapse?

options.A: Permanently removing the uterus without surgery
options.B: Relieving uncomfortable pelvic pressure
options.C: Preventing further descent of pelvic organs
options.D: Strengthening the pelvic floor muscles

explanation: Conservative management cannot remove the uterus; its goal is symptom relief and muscle strengthening without surgery. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h6)

question: When should pelvic floor muscle exercises be introduced to help prevent long-term pelvic laxity?

options.A: Following a confirmed diagnosis of third-degree prolapse
options.B: Only after the onset of menopause
options.C: During the antenatal and postnatal periods
options.D: Immediately prior to a major pelvic surgery

explanation: Early education on pelvic floor exercises during pregnancy and after birth helps tone and protect supportive muscles. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h7)

question: How does preventing chronic constipation help protect a woman from uterine prolapse?

options.A: It improves the absorption of estrogen in the large bowel
options.B: It prevents infections from ascending into the vaginal canal
options.C: It directly strengthens the cardinal ligaments of the uterus
options.D: It stops repeated straining that increases downward abdominal pressure

explanation: Straining during bowel movements exerts downward pressure on the pelvic floor, which can weaken supports over time. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary medical term for painful menstrual cramps?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Metrorrhagia

explanation: Dysmenorrhea is the specific medical term used to describe painful menstruation that interferes with a woman's daily activities. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria delay seeking care for severe menstrual pain?

options.A: Severe pain is often wrongly viewed as a normal part of being a woman
options.B: Traditional herbs completely cure all forms of pelvic pain
options.C: Hospitals charge very high fees specifically for menstrual cramps
options.D: Midwives are legally barred from discussing menstrual disorders

explanation: Cultural normalization of menstrual pain leads many women and families to suffer in silence without seeking professional medical help. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which chemical substance released by the endometrium is the primary cause of pain in primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prostaglandins
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Excessive prostaglandin production causes the uterus to contract strongly, reducing blood flow and resulting in crampy pain. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h2)

question: When does primary dysmenorrhea most commonly first appear in a young woman's life?

options.A: During menopause when hormone levels begin to fluctuate wildly
options.B: Shortly after ovulatory cycles become established following menarche
options.C: Years before her very first menstrual period begins
options.D: Only after she has given birth to her first child

explanation: Primary dysmenorrhea usually appears within the first year or two after a girl starts menstruating, once her cycles become regularly ovulatory. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of secondary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Adenomyosis
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.C: Primary hormonal fluctuation
options.D: Uterine fibroids

explanation: Primary hormonal fluctuation drives normal cycles and primary dysmenorrhea, whereas secondary dysmenorrhea is caused by distinct structural or inflammatory conditions like fibroids. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h3)

question: What clinical feature strongly points toward secondary dysmenorrhea rather than primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Normal pelvic examination findings with no uterine tenderness
options.B: Pain starting for the first time in a woman in her late thirties
options.C: Cramps lasting for only forty-eight hours during bleeding
options.D: Mild nausea accompanying the first day of menstruation

explanation: New-onset dysmenorrhea appearing later in life, well past adolescence, is a classic sign of an acquired secondary pelvic pathology. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the very first step a midwife should take when evaluating a client presenting with painful periods?

options.A: Prescribe high-dose opioid pain relievers
options.B: Perform an immediate pregnancy test without asking questions
options.C: Immediately schedule an exploratory laparoscopy
options.D: Take a detailed menstrual and medical history

explanation: A thorough history is the essential first step to understand the pain pattern and differentiate between primary and secondary causes. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why must a midwife always rule out pregnancy before starting medical treatment for pelvic pain?

options.A: Pregnant women never experience any form of pelvic or abdominal discomfort
options.B: Pregnancy completely cures all forms of primary and secondary dysmenorrhea
options.C: Many common pain medications and treatments can harm an early developing pregnancy
options.D: Hospitals in Nigeria prohibit giving any medication to women of childbearing age

explanation: Because NSAIDs and hormonal therapies can be teratogenic or cause complications, pregnancy must be ruled out first. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which class of medication is considered the first-line pharmaceutical treatment for primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Strong narcotic opioids
options.B: Skeletal muscle relaxants
options.C: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.D: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: NSAIDs directly target the production of prostaglandins, which are the main culprits behind primary dysmenorrhea pain. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h5)

question: How do combined oral contraceptive pills help reduce menstrual cramp pain?

options.A: By paralyzing the nerves that transmit pain signals to the brain
options.B: By suppressing ovulation and keeping the endometrial lining thin
options.C: By directly destroying uterine fibroids within the pelvic cavity
options.D: By permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles forever

explanation: Oral contraceptives prevent ovulation and reduce the thickness of the endometrium, which lowers the overall amount of prostaglandins produced. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h5)

question: What advice should a midwife give a client regarding when to take her prescribed NSAID for menstrual cramps?

options.A: Take the medication at the very onset of bleeding or right before pain starts
options.B: Wait until the pain becomes unbearable before taking any pill
options.C: Take the medication only after the menstrual period has completely ended
options.D: Take the pills exclusively during the middle of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Taking NSAIDs early prevents prostaglandins from building up and causing severe contractions, making pain control much more effective. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is a warning sign that requires a client with dysmenorrhea to seek immediate medical review?

options.A: Needing to rest for an hour on the first day
options.B: Mild fatigue on the first day of her period
options.C: A slight decrease in energy levels during menses
options.D: Sudden high fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge

explanation: Fever and foul discharge suggest an underlying pelvic infection like PID, which needs urgent medical diagnosis and antibiotic treatment. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h6)

question: What blood loss amount is traditionally used to define heavy menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Greater than 80 milliliters
options.B: Exactly 50 milliliters
options.C: Less than 30 milliliters
options.D: More than 200 milliliters

explanation: Clinical guidelines set the lower limit for heavy menstrual bleeding at 80 milliliters per cycle. In practice, midwives rely more on how the patient describes their daily symptoms and impact on life. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do many women wait a long time before seeking help for heavy periods?

options.A: Symptoms only occur once every year
options.B: They assume their heavy flow is normal
options.C: Blood clots dissolve before leaving the body
options.D: Anemia completely prevents them from traveling

explanation: Because heavy periods often run in families or have happened since their very first period, many women accept heavy bleeding as their normal baseline. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of these conditions is considered a structural cause of heavy menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Uterine fibroids
options.B: Copper intrauterine device
options.C: Von Willebrand disease
options.D: Ovulatory dysfunction

explanation: Uterine fibroids, also called leiomyomas, are structural changes in the uterus. They are categorized under the PALM part of the FIGO classification system. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do copper intrauterine devices (IUDs) typically affect a woman's period?

options.A: They increase local endometrial bleeding
options.B: They shrink the size of the myometrium
options.C: They stop ovulation completely
options.D: They correct underlying blood clotting issues

explanation: Copper IUDs can cause heavier periods because of local inflammatory effects on the inner lining of the uterus. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the first-choice imaging test to check for structural causes like fibroids?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray
options.B: Computed tomography scan
options.C: Pelvic ultrasound
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: Pelvic ultrasound is safe, easy to access, and the best first-line scan for viewing the structures inside the pelvis. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h3)

question: A teenager has had severe heavy periods ever since her very first cycle. Along with a blood count, which test is most important?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy
options.B: Hysterosalpingography
options.C: Coagulation screen
options.D: Cervical cytology smear

explanation: When heavy bleeding starts right from menarche, it often points to an underlying clotting disorder like von Willebrand disease, making a coagulation screen essential. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which medication works by helping blood to clot, directly reducing heavy menstrual flow?

options.A: Progesterone cream
options.B: Combined estrogen pills
options.C: Ibuprofen tablets
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic medicine. It stabilizes blood clots in the vessels of the uterus to slow down bleeding. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system often used to treat heavy periods?

options.A: It directly thins the endometrial lining locally
options.B: It immediately boosts systemic iron stores
options.C: It completely cures systemic blood clotting disorders
options.D: It permanently removes all uterine fibroids

explanation: The device releases progestin directly into the uterus, keeping the lining thin and greatly reducing menstrual blood loss over time. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which vitamin can midwives recommend taking with iron supplements to help the body absorb the iron better?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Vitamin C creates an acidic environment in the digestive tract, which helps the body absorb oral iron tablets much more effectively. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which symptom in a patient with heavy periods needs urgent medical attention?

options.A: Mild abdominal bloating
options.B: Slight darkening of stool color
options.C: Dizziness and lightheadedness
options.D: Occasional breast tenderness

explanation: Dizziness is a sign of significant blood loss and possible severe anemia, which requires a prompt clinical checkup. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does the term 'metrorrhagia' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Painful uterine cramping without any abnormal bleeding
options.B: Excessive blood loss strictly during regular monthly periods
options.C: Complete absence of menstrual bleeding for six months
options.D: Bleeding that happens at irregular, unpredictable times

explanation: Metrorrhagia refers specifically to uterine bleeding that occurs at random and unexpected times between normal menstrual cycles. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T4#BMP310_U3_T4_h1)

question: How is metrorrhagia different from menorrhagia?

options.A: Metrorrhagia causes severe pelvic pain, while menorrhagia is completely painless
options.B: Metrorrhagia is irregular timing, while menorrhagia is heavy flow on a regular schedule
